### Decisions the plan did not settle

1. **`dev-console` exists only when `E2E_DEV_CONSOLE=true`**, instead of being always listed (item above). The alternative, listing it and passing `--project=chromium --project=locales` in the existing step, would change that step and break when T24 adds its project.
2. **The 404 routes' own document is excused by a rule, not by a list entry**, because it is the browser's message about a page that is meant to be a 404, not Next's or React's dev validation. The rule is narrow (type, exact text, the route's own URL, expected status 404).
3. **The favicon is a placeholder file**, not a design choice: the brand icon is yours.
4. **`stop-tree.sh`** instead of `kill "$pid"`: see "How it runs".
5. **The dev server's log is uploaded, not judged.** It was clean; a check on it would need its own list of excused lines.
6. **The browser's console only.** Server-side `console.error` calls reach it in dev (the mutation above), which is why the market layout is covered.
7. **One visit per route**, no client navigation between routes. A navigation test (links, prefetch) would be a new check; the DS pages' viewport switcher and the locale toggle are not clicked here.

The two CI steps' `run` scripts, taken out of `ci.yml` and run in order with `RUNNER_TEMP` set: **normal path 12 passed**, ports free and nothing left in `ps`. **Mutation (a)**: a `next start` kept alive by a restarting supervisor, with a dead PID in `storefront.pid`: the step fails with exit 1 at `stop-tree.sh` ("port 8000 still accepts connections"), before any test. **Mutation (a′)**: the same with a `stop-tree.sh` that exits 0 like the old one: the step fails with "next dev exited before it answered" (`next dev` dies of EADDRINUSE), so the readiness check alone also refuses it. Tools the scripts use: `bash`, `ps`, `awk`, `curl`, and for a port's owner any of `lsof`, `ss`, `fuser`; on this VM `lsof` sees no sockets and `fuser` does, which is why all that exist are asked. ### What was done

1. **`components.json`, both, by hand** (shadcn's monorepo page): `style: "base-vega"` (D29), `baseColor: "neutral"`, `iconLibrary: "lucide"`, `rsc: true`, `tailwind.config: ""`, `tailwind.css` at `packages/ui/src/styles/globals.css`, the aliases `ui` and `components` → `@shopblok/ui/atoms`, `utils` → `@shopblok/ui/lib/utils`, `hooks` → `@shopblok/ui/hooks`, `lib` → `@shopblok/ui/lib`, and `registries: { "@reui": "https://reui.io/r/{style}/{name}.json" }`. `packages/ui` exports `./atoms/*` (`.tsx`), `./lib/*`, `./hooks/*`, `./globals.css` and `./tokens`; no barrel.
2. **`cn` is shadcn's own package now.** In shadcn 4.21.4's `base-vega` registry every item imports `cn` from `"cn"` (npm `cn` 0.4.0, MIT, by shadcn and Aiden Bai, 2026-09-22: "a drop-in replacement for clsx + tailwind-merge", zero dependencies), and the style's `index` item lists `cn`, `class-variance-authority`, `lucide-react` and `@base-ui/react`; `clsx` and `tailwind-merge` are not used. The CLI rewrites that import whatever `utils` says. I kept D30's `src/lib/utils.ts` as `export { cn } from "cn";` and pointed the atoms at it, so a custom Tailwind theme (`cn/config`'s `createCn`) has one place to go; `clsx` and `tailwind-merge` (plan §2) are not installed.
3. **The CLI did not install anything and did not resolve the aliases at first.** `shadcn add` from `apps/storefront` needs the aliases in a tsconfig: both tsconfigs now map `@shopblok/ui/{atoms,lib,hooks}` and `…/*` to `packages/ui/src/…` (the bare forms are what the CLI resolves; a wildcard `@shopblok/ui/*` was avoided because it would also capture `./globals.css` and `./tokens`). Without `src/lib/utils.ts` on disk the CLI added `cn@^0.4.0` to `packages/ui` and no other dependency; with it, none. The dependencies were then added by hand at the plan's pins: `@base-ui/react` 1.9.0, `class-variance-authority` 0.7.1, `lucide-react` 1.56.0 (1.58.0 is out, Renovate's weekly rule takes it), `cn` 0.4.0, all exact. The CLI said it "updated" `globals.css` and changed nothing in it.
4. **No `shadcn/tailwind.css`.** The style's `index` item would import it (custom variants such as `data-open` that also match Radix's `data-state`, and shimmer and scroll-fade utilities) and needs `shadcn` as a dependency. Tailwind 4's own `data-*` variants match what Base UI sets, so it is left out; every atom state was checked in Chromium. Except two: Separator's `data-horizontal:` and `data-vertical:` match nothing Base UI renders (it sets `data-orientation`), so they are written `data-[orientation=…]:` (PR 42 review, finding 1).
5. **Each atom, edited** (the header of each file lists its edits): no `dark:` classes (in Tailwind 4 they follow the OS setting, and the tokens are light only, D27); `focus-visible:ring-ring` instead of `ring-ring/50`; `pl-`/`pr-`/`ml-`/`right-`/`left-`/`text-left` → `ps-`/`pe-`/`ms-`/`end-`/`start-`/`text-start`; Tooltip and Select take only `top`, `bottom`, `inline-start` and `inline-end` (a type: `left` and `right` would need physical classes); NativeSelect's options use the popover tokens instead of `Canvas`/`CanvasText`; Spinner's hard-coded `aria-label="Loading"` is a required `label` prop (D30), fed from `catalogs.*.atoms.spinner.loading`; Skeleton is `aria-hidden` and pulses with `motion-safe:`.
6. **D32, 44 px.** Button: `min-h-11` (default), `min-h-12` (`lg`), `size-11`/`size-12` (`icon`, `icon-lg`); `xs`, `sm`, `icon-xs` and `icon-sm` are gone. Input, Select's trigger and NativeSelect: `h-11`, no `sm`; each Select option `min-h-11`; Textarea is `min-h-16`. Checkbox and Radio keep the kit's 16 px and Switch its 32 × 18.4 px track; each has a `::after` hit area centred on it (`-inset-3.5` → 44 × 44; the switch 44 × 44.4), and the DS entries put them in a `Label` with `min-h-11`, which is the target T24 measures. In Chromium, every button, field, combobox and label-wrapped choice in the 17 frames is at least 44 × 44 at 375, 768 and 1440 px in all four locales.
7. **Long labels wrap.** Button and Badge lost `whitespace-nowrap` (a German "In den Warenkorb legen und weiter zur Kasse" is the case), Label is `leading-snug` instead of `leading-none`, Select's options wrap. Two atoms cut on purpose and say so with `data-truncate` (D34): Select's chosen value (one line, ellipsis) and NativeSelect (the browser cuts the chosen option). Select's trigger is `max-w-full`, so it never outgrows a block container; a grid with an `auto` track still grows to its min-content, so the DS `Field` uses `grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)]`.
8. **Destructive is solid.** The kit's tinted destructive (`bg-destructive/10 text-destructive`) is **4.01:1** on white, 3.31:1 at the hover's 20 %: below 4.5:1. Button and Badge draw `bg-destructive text-destructive-foreground` (4.77:1, T19's override 4), hover darkens with `color-mix` against `foreground`.
9. **Tests** (Vitest 5.0.3, happy-dom 21.0.1, Testing Library 16.3.3 / 10.4.2 / user-event 14.6.8): for each atom its role and name, focus by Tab, disabled, `aria-invalid`, the 44 px classes and a long German and Greek label from `@shopblok/fixtures`; Space toggles Checkbox (Enter does not) and Switch; the arrows move through RadioGroup and skip a disabled radio, Tab leaves the group; Select opens with ArrowDown, moves and picks with Enter; Tooltip opens on focus and hover and closes on Escape. `class-rules.test.ts` scans every `src/atoms/*.tsx` (strings only, comments stripped) and checks each file starts with a source header; its own cases cover each rule both ways. Type tests (`@ts-expect-error`): no `sm` button size, Spinner's `label` required, no `side="left"`.
10. **DS entries** (`src/design-system/atoms.tsx`, spread into `entries`): 17 pages × 4 locales, each with a live render and its states (default, focus, disabled, invalid and long label for fields; hover only on Button). Hover and focus can't be held on a static page, so those states draw the classes `:hover` and `:focus-visible` add, and say so. Every sample string is from the fixtures, which gained `optionLabel`, `toggleLabel`, `badge`, `hint`, `personName`, `progressLabel` (ordinary and long, four locales) and `shortcut` (`Strg` + `K` in German). `icons.ts` lists Check, ChevronDown, ChevronUp, Loader2 and Heart (a sample icon), and the credits name shadcn/ui, Base UI and Lucide.
11. **`check:workspace`** checks `packages/ui`: React 19.3.0, `@types/react` 19, and the React that `@base-ui/react` resolves. React, React DOM and their types are peers and dev dependencies, `next` 16.4.0 a peer (D30).
12. **`dev-console.spec.ts`** opens `/design-system/{en,el,de,fr}/atoms/select` (the atom with the most client code). **`styles-fonts.spec.ts`**'s `@source` check looks for the Switch's `after:-inset-y-[13px]`, and `source-probe.ts` is deleted, as T20 asked.
13. **NOTICE.md:** shadcn/ui (MIT), `cn` (MIT), Base UI (MIT), ReUI (MIT, for T23's items), Lucide (ISC) and the kit (CC BY 4.0). **Renovate:** `lucide-react` in both packages as one group, before 6 am on Mondays.

### Decisions the plan did not settle

1. **`cn` instead of `clsx` + `tailwind-merge`** (item 2), because the registry writes it.
2. **The hit areas are `::after`, the measured target is the label** (item 6). A pseudo-element counts for clicks but not for `getBoundingClientRect`, so T24's size check should measure a Checkbox, Radio or Switch through its `label`.
3. **Solid destructive** (item 8) and **wrapping buttons** (item 7) depart from the kit's look; both were needed for D35's 4.5:1 and D34's no-clipping rule.
4. **Logical sides only** on Tooltip and Select (item 5).
5. **The atoms' copy is small:** `atoms.spinner.loading` is the only string an atom itself needs; the rest of what the entries show is sample content and lives in the fixtures, as T22 set up.
6. **Prettier:** the vendored files are formatted with the repo's preset (`packages/config/prettier.config.mjs`), so they carry semicolons and 100 columns; a later `shadcn add --overwrite` will undo that and the edits, so diff before accepting one.

### Smaller observations

- `@base-ui/react`'s optional peers `date-fns` and `@date-fns/tz` were already in the lockfile (another package brings them), so pnpm links them; nothing imports them.
- Base UI's Checkbox, Radio and Switch render a `span` with the role and a hidden 1 × 1 `input`; happy-dom handles both, and Space, the arrows and label clicks behave there as in Chromium.
- The CLI printed "Remember to wrap your app with `TooltipProvider`". The Tooltip DS entry wraps its own; M2's layout should add one at the root.

| 6 | Spinner's `role="status"` is unlikely to be announced | A line in its a11y notes: in a button the button's name carries it; a loading area takes `aria-busy` or text in a live region already on the page |

### How it works

1. **The atoms come from the page** (until T29: the spec now imports `@shopblok/registry`, "The registry (T29)"). Playwright's loader cannot import `entries.tsx` (`next/image` resolves only inside Next), so the spec reads `/design-system/en` once at collection and takes every `/design-system/en/atoms/<slug>` link; that page is rendered from the manifest, so a new atom is checked without touching the spec. The widths are `viewportWidths()`, the DS's own.
2. **The flag.** If `/design-system/en` is not 200, the suite is one test, "the build serves the design system", which fails with `… answered 404, not 200: this build lacks DESIGN_SYSTEM_ENABLED=true (the DS routes are 404 without it, D33) …`.
3. **Each cell** attaches its screenshot first, then runs the four checks with `expect.soft`, so one cell reports every failed check:
   - **axe** (`@axe-core/playwright`, tags `wcag2a`, `wcag2aa`, `wcag21a`, `wcag21aa`, `wcag22aa`): no violations, printed with selectors and axe's summary.
   - **overflow:** `scrollWidth` ≤ `innerWidth`, and no element with hidden or clipped overflow has `scrollWidth > clientWidth` outside `[data-truncate]`. Two exemptions, both found on the first run (18 failures, all overflow): visually hidden boxes (1 × 1 or `.sr-only`, such as Base UI's hidden inputs and Progress's label), and a clipped element with no text (Rating's partial-star mask); an input's value counts as text.
   - **size (D32):** buttons, standalone links, inputs, selects, textareas and the control roles are at least 44 × 44, counting a control's `::after` hit area from its resolved inset; Checkbox, Radio and Switch also pass by their label. Skipped: `aria-hidden`, `display: none`, `visibility: hidden`, ≤ 1 × 1, and a link inline with its parent's own text (WCAG 2.5.8's exemption).
   - **console:** `e2e/support/console.ts`'s rules (T25 had already moved them out of `payload-admin.spec.ts`), and failed requests to the server.
4. **The project** exists only with `E2E_DESIGN_SYSTEM=true`, as `dev-console` does, retries 0; the `chromium` project ignores the spec. `PW_CHROMIUM_PATH` points Playwright at a local Chromium (this VM's `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome`) and is unset in CI.
5. **The job** (ubuntu, Node 22, 30 min limit, beside `e2e-smoke`): install, Playwright's Chromium, `pnpm --filter @shopblok/storefront build` with `DESIGN_SYSTEM_ENABLED=true` (not through turbo), `next start` with its PID kept, a wait for `/design-system/en` (120 s), the project, `stop-tree.sh`, and two artifacts: `design-system-report` (the HTML report and `test-results`, one PNG per cell, so six per atom) and the server log. No compose, no bootstrap, no `.env`: the flagged build ran here with none of them in about 35 s.
6. **`@axe-core/playwright` is 4.13.0**, not the latest 4.14.0: that was published the day before and pnpm's minimum release age refused it. Renovate will offer it.

### Mutations

Each applied, run at `en · 375`, and reverted.

| Mutation | Check | Output |
|---|---|---|
| Price drawn in `#bbbbbb` | axe | `color-contrast (serious) … insufficient color contrast of 1.91 … Expected contrast ratio of 4.5:1` |
| Chip at `width: 500px; max-width: none` | overflow | `the page is wider than the viewport (scrollWidth 533, innerWidth 375)` |
| Button's `min-h-11` as `min-h-9` | size | `controls smaller than 44 × 44 (D32)` / `button[data-slot=button]"Add to cart": its hit area 108.3 × 38.0` |
| `console.error` in Checkbox's effect | console | `error @ /design-system/en/frame/atoms/checkbox: mutation: console.error in checkbox` |
| A build without the flag | flag | one test, `answered 404, not 200: this build lacks DESIGN_SYSTEM_ENABLED=true …` |

### Decisions the plan did not settle

1. The two overflow exemptions above, instead of putting `data-truncate` on a star mask that truncates nothing.
2. The atoms are read from the overview page rather than a list in the spec, so the spec cannot fall behind the manifest.
3. The job is not a required check: branch protection is not available on the owner's plan (G3).

### Code-review fixes (PR 44)

The review is `reviews/pr-44-code-review.md`. Findings 1 to 8 were fixed; 9 and 10 (a composite action for starting the storefront, a table of opt-in projects) are optional refactors left for when a third opt-in project or a third copy of the start steps appears.

| # | Finding | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Vertical clipping was never caught | Each axis is checked on its own (`overflowX` with the widths, `overflowY` with the heights, 1 px for rounding). Mutation: Badge at `h-3 overflow-y-hidden` fails with `scrollHeight 15 > clientHeight 10; text "Νέο"` |
| 2 | `::after` counted against the wrong containing block | The hit area is used only when the control is positioned; otherwise its own box |
| 3 | An ancestor's `visibility: hidden` skipped a visible control | Only the element's own computed `visibility` counts; `display: none` and `aria-hidden` still hide the subtree |
| 4 | An id other than one `[a-z0-9-]+` segment dropped out silently | Any id under `atoms/` is taken |
| 5 | Links between separators counted as running text | The parent's text must hold a letter or a digit |
| 6 | `E2E_DESIGN_SYSTEM` replaced the default run silently | Both flags at once throw; set them per command (`E2E_DESIGN_SYSTEM=true pnpm --filter @shopblok/storefront test:e2e --project=design-system`), not exported |
| 7 | One worker | Two for the `design-system` project (static pages, no login): 3.0 min locally |
| 8 | The collection's `fetch` had no timeout | 30 s, reported as the suite's one failing test |

**Proof.** `tsc`, `eslint`, then the full project against a fresh flagged build: 192 passed.

## Backend outage (S4)

**Result: S4 passes as the plan defines it, so [ADR 0004](adr/0004-catalog-data-in-the-shell.md) is *Accepted* with D36 as the owner chose it on 2026-10-14.** A product page that reads Medusa in its static shell (variant B: `cached()`, `notFound()` before any `Suspense`, `generateStaticParams` from Medusa with a build stand-in, `ensureStatic = "navigation"`) keeps serving the last good page while Medusa is down (O2), answers **500** for a page it never rendered (O3) and a real **404** for a missing product (O4), recovers with no restart (O5), builds in CI's state with a stand-in (O6), refuses to build when its backend URL is set and Medusa is down (O7), and is `○` in the build output (O9). `/next/status` (variant C) answers 503 within 2.01 s in every outage case (O8). The variant the wiring page uses today (A) answers 200 with the error state (O10), as T12 found. **Six readings came out of it** (ADR 0004, "Decision"): the export `ensureStatic = "navigation"` is needed (without it, B2, the first answers are 200); with it, a per-visitor part cannot read `cookies()` on the server even inside `Suspense` (B3 fails the build), so the header cart count and other per-visitor parts on catalog pages read in the browser (B4); a URL left without traffic for longer than `expire` gives one 500 during an outage, so the catalog's `expire` is long; CI's `e2e-smoke` has to start Medusa before `pnpm build` once the first catalog page exists; `/next/status` must read the Store API, because **Medusa's `/health` answers 200 while its database is down**; and the 404 and 500 bodies are Next's bare error shell, with the not-found page or the error state rendered after hydration.

### What should change in the plan

1. **D36 holds**, with ADR 0004's six readings. The plan's D36 row says so, and §8 item 16 lists the spec lines for T26 (ADR 0004, "Spec changes": §8.1's table and paragraph, §8.3's per-visitor parts and `expire`, §12, §14's CI order, §17.1).
2. **For M2:** the header's cart count and any per-visitor molecule on a catalog page are Client Components that read in the browser. The prototype's `useEffect` and `setState` tripped `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` and carried a disable; the real one should use `useSyncExternalStore` or a data hook.
3. **For M3:** `ensureStatic = "navigation"` on the home, PDP and PLP; `generateStaticParams` with the stand-in rule and its unit test; a long `expire` with tags; `e2e-smoke` starts Medusa before `pnpm build`; the Playwright outage test (stop Medusa by PID: O2's 200, O3's 5xx, O4's 404, `/next/status` 503); `/next/status` with the Store API read.
4. **For M7:** repeat O2, O3 and the expiry check on a Vercel preview; point the monitors at `/next/status`.
5. **For the owner, the cloud environment:** the setup script's last run had no network, so the saved copy has no pnpm 12.10.1, no compose images, no Chromium in `/opt/ms-playwright`, and no `/opt/dtc-starter` or `/opt/payload-templates`. It runs again after a change to the script or the allowed domains; check `grep -E 'setup (start|end)|step 6' /var/log/shopblok-setup.log` at the start of the next session. CLOUD.md now has the session's workarounds.

### Smaller observations

- **`next start`'s log had `MaxListenersExceededWarning: Possible EventEmitter memory leak detected. 11 close listeners added to [ServerResponse]`** three times, at start-up and under the probes. Not traced; it may be on `main` too.
- **Prettier reads `[market]` in a path as a glob character class:** `prettier --check "…/[market]/spike-product/**"` finds no file; pass the directory without `/**`.
- **The `next-server` process of a stopped `next start` can stay as a zombie** (`<defunct>`) until its parent exits; it holds no port.
- **The probes' timing:** B's prerendered pages answered in 4 to 20 ms, a first visit to an unlisted product in 126 ms with Medusa up, and the 500 for a never-rendered product in 300 ms (Medusa refused the connection at once).

## The wait for networkidle (PR 48)

**Result: `dev-console.spec.ts` waits 30 s at most for `networkidle`, then names the requests still open.** PR 48 changes only docs, and its `e2e-smoke` failed twice in its last step, "Console of the storefront in next dev" ([run 38985341436](https://github.com/stephanos221/shopblok-starter/actions/runs/38985341436), attempts 1 and 2). The same step passed on `main` an hour before (run 38981232705).

| | Attempt 1 | Attempt 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Routes that hung on the first try | `/`, typography in `en`, `el` and `de`, Select in `fr` | `/`, `/ch/fr`, typography in `el`, Select in `en` |
| Of those, also on the retry | typography in `en` and `de` | typography in `el` |
| How they failed | `Test timeout of 90000ms exceeded`, at `page.waitForLoadState("networkidle")` | the same |

- Every try that finished saw 0 console messages and no failed request, and the retries passed in 4 to 15 s.
- `next dev`'s log answers every request of a hung try in under 2 s, with no error, so what stayed open was in the browser.
- **Off the runner it does not happen.** A probe recorded every request on the same routes in `next dev`:
  - it reached `networkidle` about 0.5 s after `load` on each, on 4 cores and on 2 (`taskset -c 0,1`, a cold `.next/dev`);
  - nothing was left open;
  - a DS page with the viewport switcher makes about 122 requests (the page, its three frame iframes and their chunks).
- The run's traces are in the `playwright-report` artifact, but this cloud session cannot download artifacts (the proxy refuses their storage host).

**The change.** `waitForIdle` waits 30 s at most, then lists the requests still open:

- one of this server's documents, scripts or stylesheets fails the test at once, because the first render may not have run, so a clean console would prove nothing;
- anything else (a font, an image, a fetch) is a warning, and the check goes on.

PR 49's review changed the rule (item 5, in "CI for M2 (T27)" below): any request to this server open 10 s or more now fails, whatever its type, and the rest are warnings.

So a hang now costs 30 s instead of 90 s, and the report says which request it was. The same function, in T27's `support/dev-console.ts`, was checked with two mutations, each started after `load` with `page.route` and `idleMs` at 5 s:

- a `fetch` that never answers: a warning (`fetch http://localhost:8000/hang-fetch (open 5 s)`), and the test passes (it fails since PR 49's review);
- a `<script>` that never answers: the test fails, naming `script http://localhost:8000/hang.js`.

A resource that never answers before `load` blocks `page.goto` itself, which is unchanged. The ten DS routes of `dev-console` passed locally with the change.

### The rules

`scripts/lib/ci-gate.ts` is a pure function from the event and the PR's changed files to `{ e2e, designSystem, windows }`, with its lists at the top and a comment on each entry. Both rules fail open: a job is skipped only when every changed file is on a list known not to affect it, and a file on no list runs it.

| Job | Skipped on a PR when every changed file is | Runs for |
|---|---|---|
| `e2e-smoke` | docs (`docs/`, any `.md`), tooling (below), or the design system's own: `packages/registry/`, `packages/ui/src/{primitives,molecules,organisms}/`, `apps/storefront/src/design-system/`, `apps/storefront/src/app/design-system/`, `e2e/design-system.spec.ts`, `e2e/dev-console-ds.spec.ts`, `e2e/__screenshots__/` | anything else, and any dependency file |
| `design-system` | docs, tooling, or a file the DS pages cannot reach: `apps/backend/`, `infra/`, `compose.yaml`, the market routes, Payload's admin, API, config, collections, types and migrations, `src/app/next/`, `src/scripts/`, the other suites' specs, unit tests and test helpers outside the DS, `.env.example`, and the root scripts other than the gate | the DS's own files, every shared package, `src/lib/`, `src/styles/`, `next.config.ts`, the Playwright config, `.github/`, the gate, anything new, and any dependency file |
| `windows-smoke` | anything but a dependency file (its rule since T16) | a `package.json` at any depth, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` |

Tooling is what only tools read, which both rules skip: every `eslint.config.mjs`, `packages/config/eslint/`, the Prettier config, every `components.json` (the shadcn CLI), every `.gitignore`, `.editorconfig` and `renovate.json`. `check` lints and formats; `next build` has not run ESLint since Next 16. `apps/storefront/.env.example` is not tooling: `pnpm bootstrap` may copy it, so it runs `e2e-smoke`.

**The import rule.** `scripts/ci-gate.ts` reads the run-time imports of every source file and stylesheet in `apps/` and `packages/` (unit tests left out; `import type` and `export type` left out, because TypeScript erases them). It matches `import … from "…"`, `export … from "…"`, a bare `import "…"`, `import("…")` and `require("…")` with a quoted or a template-literal path (up to its first `${`, so a template that starts with `${`, or names only the package as in `@shopblok/ui/${folder}/x`, is not seen), and a stylesheet's `@import "…"` or `@import url("…")`. A DS-only area that a file outside every DS-only area imports, by its package name (`@shopblok/ui/molecules/…`, `@shopblok/registry`) or by a relative path, counts as shared: a change in it runs `e2e-smoke` too. A file inside a shared area counts as outside, and the pass repeats until nothing is added, so a market page that imports an organism also shares the molecules the organism imports (PR 49 review, item 1). Today nothing outside the DS imports them, so the scan finds nothing; M3's pages and M4's Payload config will be the first.

**Other events.** A push to `main` runs `e2e-smoke` and `design-system` but not `windows-smoke`, as `windows-gate` did since T16: the PR that was merged ran it if it changed a dependency file, and a Windows run bills about 36 minutes. The plan's T27 step 2 first said a push runs all three; D53 also said `windows-smoke` keeps its rule, and the plan now says the rule wins. The schedule, a dispatch and any event the gate does not know run all three.

**The job.** Checkout, `actions/setup-node` from `.nvmrc`, `node scripts/ci-gate.ts`: no pnpm and no install, because the script uses Node's built-ins only. It reads the PR's files with `gh api --paginate` (both names of a rename), prints one line per job with the file that decided it, and writes `e2e`, `design-system` and `windows` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`. If it fails, the three jobs behind it are skipped and the run is red. Locally, `node scripts/ci-gate.ts --files <paths>` prints the decision for a list of files.

### The DS pages in `next dev`

`e2e-smoke`'s last step checked eleven DS routes in `next dev` beside the storefront's six (T25). They need no stack, so they moved to a project of their own, `dev-console-ds` (`e2e/dev-console-ds.spec.ts`), which the `design-system` job runs after its checks: stop `next start` with `stop-tree.sh`, start `next dev` with the start action (which proves the answer comes from a dev server, as T25's step did), run the project, stop `next dev`. `next dev` shows the DS without the flag (development). The check itself (a page per route, the console rules, the excuses) moved unchanged from `dev-console.spec.ts` into `e2e/support/dev-console.ts`, and each spec is now a list of routes. `e2e-smoke`'s `dev-console` keeps `/`, `/us`, `/ch/fr`, `/el-cy`, `/nope/nope` and `/next/markets`. Both projects exist under `E2E_DEV_CONSOLE=true`, chosen with `--project`.

Locally, in CI's state (no `.env`, no stack): `COMMAND=dev URL=http://localhost:8000/design-system/en` through the action's script answered in 9.6 s, and `E2E_DEV_CONSOLE=true pnpm --filter @shopblok/storefront test:e2e --project=dev-console-ds` passed 10 of 10 in 1.2 min with 0 console messages; `stop-tree.sh` then freed port 8000.

**The wait for `networkidle` now also says what kept the network busy.** PR 48 bounded the wait at 30 s ("The wait for networkidle (PR 48)" above). On its green run ([38988638454](https://github.com/stephanos221/shopblok-starter/actions/runs/38988638454)) one route timed out at that margin with no request open: `/design-system/el/atoms/select: no networkidle within 30 s; open requests: none`, and then passed, with 0 console messages. That fits two causes: something started a request at least every 500 ms (Playwright's rule for `networkidle`), or the browser's count of open requests disagreed with its own events. The check moved with the rest into `support/dev-console.ts`, and its report now ends with the requests that started in the last 5 s, counted by URL, so the next time-out tells the two apart, and then with the page's frames (URL, and whether each is detached), because `networkidle` counts every frame's requests and a DS page with the viewport switcher has three lazy iframes (PR 49 review, item 6; inferred, not reproduced). Since the review, any request to this server open 10 s or more fails the test, whatever its type (item 5): `next dev` answered every request on the runner in under 2 s, so one that hangs is a bug (a route handler or a server action that never answers), and the time-out with nothing open stays a warning.

### The start action and the opt-in projects (PR 44 review, items 9 and 10)

- **`.github/actions/start-storefront`:** inputs `command` (`start` or `dev`), `url` (must answer 200), `name` (the log and PID files in `$RUNNER_TEMP/servers`) and `timeout` (120 s). It starts the server with `nohup … &`, writes the PID file, and waits with `curl` and `kill -0` as the three copies did; for `dev` it also waits for `/_next/static/development/_buildManifest.js`. On a time-out it stops the tree and fails. A server's environment (`E2E_TEST_ROUTES`) goes in the calling step's `env`. Stopping stays `stop-tree.sh`, in `if: always()` steps that skip a server whose PID file is missing. `e2e-smoke` now starts Medusa first and waits for `/health`, then the storefront: the two waits used to share one loop.
- **`playwright.config.ts`:** a table of `{ flag, workers, projects }`. `E2E_DEV_CONSOLE` holds `dev-console` and `dev-console-ds` (one worker, one retry), `E2E_DESIGN_SYSTEM` holds `design-system` (two workers). Two flags at once still throw (item 6), and the default projects ignore every opt-in spec, so a new opt-in project is one row. `playwright test --list` gives the same tests as before for the default run and both flags.

### Review fixes (PR 49)

| 1 | A DS-only folder imported only through another (a page, an organism, its molecules) stayed DS-only | `sharedAreas` repeats until nothing is added; an importer inside a shared area counts as outside. | 2 | A failed DS check skipped the DS pages' `next dev` check | "Start next dev" runs when the checks ran (passed or failed) and `next start` was stopped (`steps.stop-start.outcome == 'success'`), and the check when `next dev` answered. Checked with `actionlint` and by reading, not with a failing run; the two Playwright runs write to separate report folders, so the checks' report survives |
| 3 | Tooling-only files ran `e2e-smoke` | One `toolingOnly` list that both rules skip (`eslint.config.mjs`, the shared ESLint and Prettier configs, `components.json`, `.gitignore`, `.editorconfig`, `renovate.json`), with a test; `.env.example` still runs `e2e-smoke`. M1's PR 38 now runs neither job |
| 4 | The scan saw only quoted imports in JS and TS | Template-literal `import(…)`/`require(…)` up to the first `${`, and stylesheets' `@import`, with a test each; the gaps that remain are named in the comment |
| 5 | A request to this server that hung was a warning unless it was a document, script or stylesheet | Any request to this server open 10 s or more fails, whatever its type (`hangMs`); younger ones and other origins stay warnings |
| 6 | A time-out with nothing open gave no clue | The report ends with the page's frames, and whether each is detached |

| Changed | `apps/storefront/next.config.ts` (`rewrites`), `src/next-config.test.ts`, `src/proxy.test.ts` (its URL lists moved to `proxy-urls.ts`, with six more), `e2e/markets.spec.ts` ("root files"), `e2e/dev-console.spec.ts` (two routes), `ci.yml` (`e2e-smoke`'s log check) |

### How it works

- **The rewrite.** `next.config.ts` has one `afterFiles` rewrite, `/:file([^/]*\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*)` → `/next/missing-file`: the proxy matcher's file rule (a last segment that ends in a dot and a letter, so `/size-8.5` is a slug) on one segment only. Next 16.4's `rewrites.md` gives the order: the proxy, `beforeFiles`, then `public/` files, `_next/static` and the routes without a dynamic segment, then `afterFiles`, then the dynamic routes. So `/favicon.ico` (a file route) and M7's `robots.ts` and `sitemap.ts` are served before the rewrite is tried, and `[market]` only after it. The proxy never sees these paths, because its matcher skips files, so nothing rewrites them to a market first.
- **The route.** `GET` answers `404`, `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8` and `Not Found`; `HEAD` the same with no body. It reads nothing, so Cache Components prerenders it (`○ /next/missing-file` in the build), and `.next/server/app/next/missing-file.meta` keeps `"status":404`. Prerendered, it was sent with `cache-control: s-maxage=31536000`, a year in a CDN; Next's own 404 page (`/next/nope`, `/us/robots.txt`) sends `private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate`, so the route sets that, and the prerendered answer carries it (measured with `curl -i` on `next start`, GET and HEAD, both `x-nextjs-cache: HIT`).
- **Not `.rsc`.** The pattern skips a last segment ending in `.rsc` (a lookahead, `(?![Rr][Ss][Cc]$)`, so `.RSC` too: Next matches the source case-insensitively but extracts its parameters case-sensitively, and with `(?!rsc$)` the helper threw "extracting params from path failed" on `/us.RSC`). Next 16.4's adapter output addresses a dynamic page's RSC payload with a `.rsc` suffix (`build-complete.js`, the dynamic routes' suffix group), and those routes run after `afterFiles`, so on a platform that turns an RSC request for `/us` into `/us.rsc` the rewrite would otherwise answer it with the text 404 (PR 50 review, item 1; inferred from Next's code, not reproduced: `next start` asks for `/us` with the `RSC` header). The proxy's own file rule (`proxy.ts`) also treats `/us.rsc` as a file and skips it; that is older than T28, and M7's first Vercel deployment should check both.
- **Why a route.** A rewrite whose destination resolves to nothing falls through to the dynamic routes, `[market]` again (`rewrites.md`; the second mutation below).
- **The tests.** `next-config.test.ts` runs the real config through `unstable_getResponseFromNextConfig` (it applies `afterFiles` rewrites by their patterns; it knows no files, so it rewrites `/favicon.ico` too, which `markets.spec.ts` covers on `next start`). On every URL of `proxy-urls.ts` it checks that the rewrite agrees with the matcher: no storefront path is rewritten, and of the paths the matcher leaves alone exactly the root files are (one segment, not Payload's, the DS's, `/next`'s, Next's or Vercel's). `markets.spec.ts` checks the answers on `next start`; `dev-console` opens `/robots.txt` and `/apple-touch-icon.png` in `next dev`, and `e2e-smoke`'s new step "No validation error in next dev's log" fails if `storefront-dev.log` has a `Could not validate` line once that run has ended (passed or failed).

## The registry (T29)

**Result: `@shopblok/registry` lists the DS's 40 entries as data (D40), and the DS page, its checks and its tests read it; `entries.tsx` is gone.** What the page says about an entry (its summary, a11y notes, live render and states) is a story in the storefront, keyed by the entry's id. Each entry also has a `preview` route (D52), and the four DS pages are `ensureStatic = "navigation"` (D44). The page looks as before: the same 192 cells pass, and the build lists the same routes plus the previews.

### How it works

- **The registry** (`packages/registry`) is data with no React: `id` (`{group}/{slug}`), `group` (`GROUPS`: `foundations`, `atoms`, `molecules`, `organisms`, `headers-footers`, SPEC §9.6's order), `kind`, `label`, `component` (`{ module: "@shopblok/ui/atoms/button", name: "Button" }`, not an import), `family` and `variant` (both or neither) and `contract` (a zod schema, D41). `defineEntries` checks the list when the module loads and throws on a malformed id, a duplicate id, an empty label, a family without a variant or a variant twice in its family, and derives `thumbnail` (`/registry/{id}.png`) for an entry with a family. Helpers: `entries`, `byGroup`, `findEntry`, `variantsOf(family)` (value, label and thumbnail, for M4's pickers). Its one dependency is `zod` 4.6.5; `sources.test.ts` reads its sources and fails on any import but `zod` and its own files.
- **The stories** (`apps/storefront/src/design-system/stories/`): one object per file, `satisfies Partial<Record<EntryId, DsStory>>`, so a story for an id the registry does not have is a type error in that file; `stories/index.ts` spreads them into a `Record<EntryId, DsStory>`, so a missing story is a type error there. `EntryId` is the union of the registry's literal ids. `stories.test.tsx` checks both ways at run time, and that every entry with a `component` names a module of `@shopblok/ui` that exports it (a dynamic import of each). `catalog.ts`'s `manifest` is the registry's entries in order, each with its story; the navigation, the params, the overview, the frames and the previews read it.
- **Props.** When an entry has a `contract`, its page shows a "Props" section before the a11y notes: the contract's top-level properties from `z.toJSONSchema`, in the schema's order, with the type (`string`, `"sale" | "new"`, `string[]`, `string | null`), whether it is required, and the description. No M1 entry has one; `props-table.test.tsx` renders a sample schema.
- **`/design-system/{locale}/preview/{id}`:** the live render alone (no states, no headings), with the frame's root layout, so the gate, the 404s and `noindex` are the frame's. T40 captures the `en` previews of the family entries as thumbnails.
- **`ensureStatic = "navigation"`** on the overview, entry, frame and preview pages: a build fails if one reads the request, even inside `<Suspense>`, where it would otherwise quietly become a partial prerender (mutations below). `routes.test.tsx` checks the four exports.
- **The checks.** `design-system.spec.ts` imports the registry (Playwright's loader reads it: it imports neither React nor `next/image`) and makes a cell of every entry outside Foundations, instead of reading the overview's links. It still opens `/design-system/en` first: with the flag off the suite is one failing test that says so.

### How to add an entry

This replaces "How T21 and T23 add an entry" (T22).

1. **The registry.** Add one object to the group's file in `packages/registry/src/entries/` (a new file for a new group, spread into `all` in `src/index.ts` in `GROUPS` order; `entries` and `EntryId` both come from `all`): `id: "molecules/product-card"`, `group`, `kind`, `label` (English, D33), `component` (`{ module: "@shopblok/ui/molecules/product-card", name: "ProductCard" }`), and `family` and `variant` if a shop picks it (D46). Its view model's schema goes in `src/contracts/` and on the entry as `contract`. The array is `as const satisfies readonly EntryInput[]`, which keeps each id a literal type.
2. **The story.** Add `"molecules/product-card": { summary, a11y, live(ctx), states }` to a file in `apps/storefront/src/design-system/stories/` (a new file is spread into `stories/index.ts`). Every sample string, price, size and colour comes from `ctx.fixture` (`@shopblok/fixtures`), money from `ctx.money`; the component's own copy is in `@shopblok/i18n`'s four catalogs (`src/messages/{en,el,de,fr}.ts`, ICU messages formatted with `formatMessage`; "View models, copy and fixtures (T30)"), and its data is a contract with fixtures. `pnpm typecheck` fails until both halves exist.
3. **Nothing else.** The navigation lists the group with its first entry (a group's label is `designSystem.groups` in `@shopblok/i18n`), the page, the frame and the preview exist in all four locales, `stories.test.tsx` renders the entry in each locale and checks its component's export, and the `design-system` job makes six cells of it (`en` and `el` at 375, 768 and 1440 px). An entry that draws an icon adds a row to `src/design-system/icons.ts`.

### Decisions the plan did not settle

1. **`kind`** is `foundation`, `atom`, `molecule` or `organism`; the headers and footers are organisms in a group of their own, so `group` alone could not say it.
2. **`component` is a reference** (module and name), checked by the storefront's test, so the registry stays loadable by Payload's CLI and Playwright.
3. **The preview pads its render by 24 px** (`p-6`), so a thumbnail does not cut a focus ring or a shadow; T40 can change it with its capture size.
4. **`entries.test.tsx` became `stories.test.tsx`**, and the foundations' stories kept `entries.tsx`'s history (`git mv`).

## View models, copy and fixtures (T30)

**Result: the 53 schemas M2's components take are in `@shopblok/registry/contracts` (D41), the copy is ICU messages in a module per locale with `formatMessage` (D43), and `@shopblok/fixtures` fills every contract in the four DS locales.** The DS page does not use the fixtures yet (the molecule tasks will), so it renders as before: the markup of the 160 entry pages (40 entries in four locales) is byte-for-byte T29's.

### How it works

- **Contracts** (`packages/registry/src/contracts/`): zod 4 schemas, each with a type of the same name (`z.infer`), imported as `@shopblok/registry/contracts`. Money is `{ amount, currencyCode }` in major units (SPEC §8.2: 29.99, never 2999); a link or an image's `src` is a root path or `http(s)`, never `//host` or `javascript:`; dates are ISO with an offset. Beyond their fields, the schemas check what a component would otherwise draw wrong: a cart's and an order's amounts are in their currency and `itemCount` is the lines' quantities; a compare-at price is higher than the price and in its currency; a rating's rows are 5 to 1 stars and add up to its count; each variant names one value of each option, every value a picture names exists, and a value id is listed once per product; an order's events are oldest first, from `placed`; a saved card is a strict object, so a card number fails the parse. `contracts.test.ts` shows each rule rejecting what it is there for, and draws every schema with `z.toJSONSchema`, as the Props table does.
- **The copy** (`packages/i18n/src/messages/`): `en.ts` is the source and its type is `Messages`; `el.ts`, `de.ts` and `fr.ts` are typed `Messages`, so a missing key is a type error. The messages are ICU (`{count, plural, one {…} other {…}}`); `formatMessage(message, values, locale)` caches a formatter per locale and message, and throws on a missing value instead of printing `{count}`. Next to it are `formatMoney`, `formatDate`, `formatNumber` and `countryName` (`Intl.DisplayNames`), each cached per locale and options. The design-system chrome is English only (D33) and lives in `design-system.ts`; `molecules` and `organisms` start empty, and each component task fills its own. `messages.test.ts` parses every message with `@formatjs/icu-messageformat-parser` and checks that each locale has English's keys and no other, that each message has English's arguments of the same kinds (a `plural` stays a plural), and that a plural uses only the language's CLDR categories (`one` and `other` in all four).
- **The fixtures** (`packages/fixtures/src/commerce/`): `commerceFixtures[locale]` is one `buildCommerceFixture` over shared data (`data/`: ids, handles, image seeds, stock, ratings, prices in EUR, USD and CHF, the category tree, the address book, orders) in the locale's words (`copy/`), so the four cannot drift apart. Each locale is its DS market: `en` the US (`/us`, USD), `el` Cyprus (no prefix, EUR), `de` Germany (`/de`, EUR), `fr` Switzerland in French (`/ch/fr`, CHF), and every link starts with that prefix. It holds 12 products (one with a title of 60 or more characters, one on sale, one sold out, one with ten swatches, one whose price varies), the Heritage Hoodie's page (4 colours × 6 sizes, some sold out), a category tree three levels deep, a cart of three lines with a promo code, an address in each of CY, US, DE and CH in its format, two orders with their events, six reviews and a rating summary, the navigation (a link, two mega menus, a dropdown) and the footer, the six seeded markets, payment methods, saved cards and shipping options (one a pickup), a search result, a filter of each kind, an announcement, a figure, and a long-string set (`long`). Dates are before `fixtureNow`, `2026-10-01T09:00:00.000Z` (D50). Pictures are `fixtureImage({ seed, ratio, alt })`: data-URI SVGs of flat shapes in 3:4, 1:1, 4:3 and 16:9, with no file, network or licence.
- **`commerce.test.ts`** parses every fixture with its contract and prints a failure with its path (`de.cart: lines.1.total.amount: …`), then checks what no schema can: the sums (line totals, subtotal, discount, the VAT inside an EU or Swiss total, the free-shipping rest, to 0.005), a summary's average against its rows, the card's rating against the page's, the prefixes, the dates, and that the German long strings are the longest.
- **The registry stays DS-only for the CI gate.** The fixtures import the contracts as types (`import type`), which TypeScript erases and the gate does not count, and the test that imports them at run time is a test, which the gate skips: `node scripts/ci-gate.ts --files packages/registry/src/contracts/product.ts` still skips `e2e-smoke`.

### How a component task uses them

1. **Its data** is a contract: extend one in `src/contracts/` or add one (exported from `contracts/index.ts`), and set it as the entry's `contract`, so the page shows its Props.
2. **Its sample data** is `commerceFixtures[ctx.locale]` (add to `data/` and `copy/` when the fixtures lack a case, and a check to `commerce.test.ts`); its long case comes from `long`.
3. **Its copy** goes in `molecules` or `organisms` of the four catalogs, as ICU, and is formatted with `formatMessage(message, values, htmlLang)`; a number, a date, a price or a country's name comes from the formatters, never from a literal.

| A changed argument (`{value}` to `{val}` in Greek's `atoms.rating.label`) | the same | no type error (both are strings); `atoms.rating.label: {"val":"argument","max":"argument"}, English {"value":"argument","max":"argument"}` |

A price multiplied by 100 is not something a schema can see (2999 is as valid as 29.99), as the plan says: Price's tests cover the formatting, and M3's resolver tests compare Medusa's raw amount with the view model.

### Decisions the plan did not settle

1. **Free shipping starts at EUR 150, USD 165 and CHF 150.** Three lines with a quantity of two, a sale and a low-stock line cannot stay under 100, so the cart (114, 126 and 113) shows a remainder of 36, 39 and 37.
2. **The sale product is the Brushed Fleece Hoodie** (49, 54, 48, from 69, 75, 67). The Heritage Hoodie keeps the DS fixtures' title, colours and description at its regular price (59, 64, 58).
3. **A pickup point's address is a `LocationAddress`**: `Address` without the person's names, the id and the default flags.
4. **`PaymentMethod.name` is what the customer reads**: a brand's own name (PayPal) or the store's translated word (Card).
5. **A category's `handle` is its own segment** (`hoodies` under Women and under Men) and its `href` carries the path. Medusa's handles are unique in the store, so M3's resolver decides how the two meet.
6. **`MarketOption.currencyCode` comes from a country-to-currency table** in the fixtures, since `markets.ts` has no currencies; M3 takes it from Medusa's regions.
7. **An order's `taxTotal` and `shippingTotal` are required** and a cart's are optional (a cart has not worked them out yet), so a US order shows a tax of 0: its price has no VAT inside, and sales tax is not modelled before M3.
8. **What the schemas leave to the tests**: sums (no schema adds up a cart) and a summary's average against its rows. Nothing stops tracking fields on an event other than `shipped`; OrderTimeline (T39) shows them where they are.
9. **The Greek, German and French copy has not been read by a native speaker.** The fixtures' and the catalogs' strings are the owner's to correct at W4.

## Primitives (T31)

**Result: the 22 primitives of D47 are in `packages/ui/src/primitives/` on our rules (20 from shadcn, `toggle` among them as `toggle-group`'s registry dependency, and ReUI's `stepper` and `timeline`); one `Providers` component (Base UI's direction, the tooltip provider, the toasts) wraps the storefront's root layout and the DS's four; and the DS draws an overlay open inside an `OverlayBox`, which a Chromium test measures.** No DS entry uses a primitive yet (D42: they appear through what uses them), so the 192 DS cells are unchanged, and they pass.

### How it works

- **Adding a primitive.** shadcn 4.21.4 ignores `-p, --path` for a `registry:ui` item: a real run writes to the `ui` alias of `packages/ui/components.json`, which is the atoms folder (T31's first real run wrote 11 files into `atoms/`; they were deleted). So, from `apps/storefront`: set `ui` and `components` to `@shopblok/ui/primitives` in **both** `components.json` files, run `pnpm dlx shadcn@4.21.4 add <item> --dry-run`, check that no atom is listed, run it for real, and put both files back. Pin what it adds (`git diff pnpm-lock.yaml`). ReUI's items are `@reui/<item>` the same way. The vendored file then gets our edits and a header that lists them.
- **Our rules, as in the atoms (D30, D32, D35, D42):** tokens only (`bg-overlay` for a backdrop, `z-(--z-modal)`, `--z-popover` and `--z-toast` for the layers), logical properties (a `side` is `inline-start` or `inline-end`, never `left` or `right`; a chevron that points along the text turns with `rtl:rotate-180`), every control 44 px (`min-h-11`, Button's `icon` size, or an `::after` hit area on a small thumb), the ring at full strength, light only. **No English:** every string a reader sees or hears is a required prop (`closeLabel` on Dialog and Sheet, `label` on Breadcrumb, Pagination and its links, the carousel's buttons and role descriptions, the toast region, `getThumbLabel` on Slider). The kit's Radix-era attributes that Base UI never sets (`data-horizontal`, `data-[state=on]`, `data-motion`) were replaced with Base UI's (`data-[orientation=…]`, `aria-pressed`, `data-activation-direction`). Each file's header says what changed in it and why it is, or is not, a client component.
- **Server components:** `accordion`, `field`, `pagination`, `table` and `toggle` have no `"use client"` (each Base UI part carries its own). `breadcrumb` and `slider` are client components since the PR 53 review (see below): BreadcrumbLink calls `useRender`, a hook, and Slider hands functions to Base UI's Thumb. Slider's `getThumbLabel` is a function too, so the component that renders it (T33's price filter) is a client component.
- **The scan** (`src/atoms/class-rules.test.ts`) now walks `atoms`, `primitives`, `molecules` and `organisms` recursively and checks the rules and the source header in each file; the atom counts stay.
- **`Providers`** (`@shopblok/ui/providers`): `DirectionProvider` (the sliders, toggle groups, menus, stepper and carousel read the direction from it, not from `<html dir>`; `dir` defaults to `ltr`, and the four store languages are all `ltr`), `TooltipProvider` (the Tooltip story no longer wraps its own) and `Toaster` (the toast manager, its portal and viewport). The market layout renders it with `catalogs[market.locale].primitives.toast`, and the DS's `Document` with the DS locale's, so the four DS root layouts have it. Any client component calls `toast.add` from `@shopblok/ui/primitives/toast`.
- **The overlay box (D45):** `OverlayBox` (`apps/storefront/src/design-system/components/`) is a box of fixed height (480 px unless given) with `[contain:paint]`, so it is the containing block of a `position: fixed` popup and clips it, and a `PortalContainerProvider` that points every primitive's portal (`usePortalContainer()`) at it. A story puts the overlay inside with `defaultOpen` and `modal={false}`, so the frame stays reachable and several open states fit on one page. The provider holds the box's **element**, from state (`ref={setBox}`), not a ref: an overlay drawn open inside the box resolves its portal before React sets a ref on the box around it, and Base UI looks again only when the prop changes, so with a ref both popups went to `<body>` (the first Chromium run found neither in its box). The check page `/design-system/{locale}/checks/overlay-box` draws a sheet and a popover open; `design-system.spec.ts` checks at 375 and 1440 px that each lies inside its box (after scrolling the box into view: a popover whose trigger is below the viewport flips above it), and runs axe on the page; the page is also in `dev-console-ds.spec.ts`.
- **The CI gate** counts `packages/ui/src/primitives/` as shared from now on, because code outside the DS imports it (the market layout renders `Providers`, which renders the toast primitive): `node scripts/ci-gate.ts --files packages/ui/src/primitives/sheet.tsx` runs `e2e-smoke` and `design-system`.

### How a component task uses them

1. Import `@shopblok/ui/primitives/<name>` and pass every label from the catalogs (`molecules` or `organisms`), never a literal.
2. A story that draws an overlay open wraps it in `<OverlayBox name="…">` with `defaultOpen` and `modal={false}`; the live render keeps the real trigger, and T33's interaction checks open it.
3. A Drawer has no close button of its own (a swipe is a gesture, and the drawer needs a way out that is not one): put a `DrawerClose` with the catalog's text in it.
4. A `DropdownMenuLabel` must sit inside a `DropdownMenuGroup` (Base UI throws otherwise).

### Decisions the plan did not settle

1. **A pressed Toggle is filled with `primary`,** and Pagination's current page is the filled `default` button. The kit's pressed `bg-muted` is 1.1:1 against the page and its current page's outline 1.26:1, under WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1.
2. **A highlighted destructive menu item is solid** `destructive` on `destructive-foreground` (4.77:1; the kit's 10 % tint is 4.01:1), as Button's destructive is.
3. **Drawer is the bottom sheet only** (`swipeDirection` `down` or `up`); a side panel is Sheet, whose `side` is `top`, `bottom`, `inline-start` or `inline-end` (default `inline-end`).
4. **`PaginationLink` is a plain `<a>`** with Button's classes: the kit's Base UI Button on an anchor gave it `role="button"`, and pagination is links (SPEC §8.4).
5. **`field` is a server component** (its error no longer memoises), so a form's layout needs no JavaScript; `navigation-menu` is a client component, because its positioner reads the portal container.
6. **Table cells wrap**, and a column that must not break (a price) takes `whitespace-nowrap` itself: the kit's `whitespace-nowrap` let one long German or Greek header widen the table.
7. **Checkbox's and Radio's hit areas were 42 px, not 44** (T21's `after:-inset-3.5` sits inside their 1 px border, which moves the containing block in by 1 px); they are now `after:-inset-[15px]`, as Slider's thumb is, and their tests measure 44.
8. **`contain: paint` is the box's containing block.** All three measured the same; it also clips, as the box's `overflow-hidden` does, and says what it is for.
9. **The toasts' region and close button are named by the catalogs** (`primitives.toast`: `Notifications` and `Close notification` in English); Base UI's default region name is English.

### Smaller observations

- **The accordion opens without its animation:** `animate-accordion-down` and `-up` come from tw-animate-css, whose keyframes read Radix's and other kits' height variables (`--radix-accordion-content-height`, falling back to `auto`) and not Base UI's `--accordion-panel-height`. T33's AccordionItem either animates the panel's height itself or drops the classes.
- **The Accordion has no arrow-key navigation between headers** in Base UI 1.9.0 (Tab moves between them); WAI-ARIA's accordion pattern makes arrows optional.
- **Toast:** Base UI marks the toasts stacked behind the front one as `aria-hidden`, close buttons included, so T33's interaction check should run axe with more than one toast open and see whether `aria-hidden-focus` is reported (not measured yet).

**CI fix (PR 53).** `windows-smoke` failed `class-rules.test.ts` "includes the primitives": on Windows `path.relative` returns `primitives\dialog.tsx`, so `startsWith("primitives/")` found none. The scanned paths are now joined with `/` on every OS.

## Product molecules (T32)

**Result: ProductCard's ten variants (D46), PriceBlock, VariantSelector, RatingSummary, ReviewItem and MediaFigure are in `packages/ui/src/molecules/`, each with its registry entry, its story, its copy in the four catalogs, fixtures and tests; Image's `sizes` is required; and the DS checks have a sixth check, controls nested in a link or a button, because axe's `nested-interactive` does not look inside a link.** The 15 new entries' 90 cells pass, and so do the 194 before them.

| | |
|---|---|
| Date | 2026-10-17 |
| Branch | prepared locally on T31 while PR 49's CI could not start, then `claude/project-thread-pmqmfo`, restarted from `main` after PR 53 merged |
| New | `packages/ui/src/molecules/{price-block, variant-selector, rating-summary, review-item, media-figure}.tsx` and their tests, `packages/ui/src/molecules/product-card/` (`parts.tsx`, one file per variant, `product-card.test.tsx`, `product-card-parts.test.tsx`), `packages/registry/src/entries/molecules.ts`, `apps/storefront/src/design-system/stories/{molecules-product-card, molecules-product}.tsx`, `molecules-product.test.tsx` |
| Changed | `packages/ui/src/atoms/{image, swatch, size-pill}.tsx` and their tests, `packages/ui/package.json` (`@shopblok/registry`, for the contract types), `packages/registry/src/{index.ts, index.test.ts, contracts/product.ts (VariantChoice), contracts/contracts.test.ts}`, `packages/i18n/src/messages/{en,el,de,fr}.ts` (`molecules.*`), `packages/fixtures/src/commerce/copy/*` (`figure.credit`), `apps/storefront/{src/design-system/{stories/index.ts, catalog.test.ts}, e2e/{design-system, dev-console-ds}.spec.ts}`, the lockfile |
| Tests | ui **1120** (490 new: ProductCard's and PriceBlock's 317, the four other molecules' 135, the rest the scan's new files, Image, Swatch and SizePill), storefront **833** (85 new: the 15 entries in four locales in `stories.test.tsx`, and `molecules-product.test.tsx`'s 25), registry **51**, fixtures 226, i18n 49, scripts 429, backend 85; `typecheck`, `lint`, `check:workspace` and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` pass |

### How it works

- **One link per card.** The title's link is the card's only link: it is `block min-h-11` (the DS size check measures the link's own box) and an `::after` stretched over the card (`after:absolute after:inset-0`) makes the whole card clickable, with the focus ring on the `::after`, around the card. Nothing between the link and the card's root is positioned, or the `::after` would cover that box instead; `overlay` puts its picture and its panel in one grid cell for that reason, and a test walks the link's ancestors in every variant. Any other control (quick add) sits outside the link and above the stretched area. A long title is clamped with `data-truncate`, and the full title stays the link's name.
- **The ten variants** share `parts.tsx` (`CardRoot`, `CardMedia`, `CardTitle`, `CardPrice`, `CardRating`, `cardBadges`, `CardSwatches`, `CardQuickAdd`) and take one set of props, `ProductCardProps`: `product` (the `ProductCard` contract), `copy` (`{ card, priceBlock }`, both from `molecules`), `locale` (the market's `<html lang>`), `sizes` (required), `heading` (`h3` unless given) and `prefetch`. Quick add also takes `action` (what a `<form action>` takes; M3 passes a server action) and `status` (`idle`, `adding`, `added`, `error`); image swap takes `swapped`, which draws the second image as on hover, because the DS runs with reduced motion and cannot hold a hover. All ten are server components.
- **PriceBlock** draws the price with the Price atom: the sale price and the struck-through original, each with its hidden label; "From {price}" for a range, as an ICU message, so a language can put the word after the price; and a tax note (`tax="included"` or `"excluded"`).
- **VariantSelector** (a client component) is one Base UI radio group per option, drawn with Swatch for a colour with a hex or an image and SizePill otherwise. Each group is named by a visible label (`aria-labelledby`, not a fieldset, so the name is not read twice) that becomes "{option}: {value}" once a value is chosen. A value is unavailable when no available variant has it together with the other options' choices; it is announced in its name and stays focusable (T23's choice, yours to change). The hidden inputs are `${name}.${optionId}`. Swatch and SizePill now take a `role` and drop `aria-pressed` under any role but `button` (axe's `aria-allowed-attr`).
- **RatingSummary** is the average (a large number, `aria-hidden`, beside the Rating atom, which carries the name), the count, and a bar per star with its count as text; with no reviews it is the message alone. **ReviewItem** is an `<article>`: the title (or the author when there is none) as its heading (`headingLevel`, 3 unless given), the author, the date (`formatDate` in UTC, never `Date.now()`), the rating, the body in paragraphs and "Verified purchase" as text. **MediaFigure** is a `<figure>` with the Image atom and a caption and credit; `sizes` is required, and `ratio` is the nearest of Image's when not given.
- **Contracts and copy (D41, D43):** packages/ui imports the contracts as types only (`import type … from "@shopblok/registry/contracts"`), so it now lists `@shopblok/registry` as a dependency. `VariantChoice` is `ProductDetail`'s options and variants with the same refinement; zod 4 forbids `.pick` on a refined object, so both are built from a shared shape and check. Every string is a catalog message under `molecules`; plurals use `one` and `other` (and `=0`).
- **The registry** lists 15 molecules (55 entries): `molecules/price-block`, `molecules/product-card-{standard, swatches, quick-add, overlay, minimal, horizontal, compact, editorial, bordered, image-swap}` (the `product-card` family, so `variantsOf("product-card")` gives the ten in that order), `variant-selector`, `rating-summary`, `review-item` and `media-figure`. The DS's navigation gains the Molecules group.
- **The DS's sixth check (`nestedControls`, `design-system.spec.ts`):** a link, a button or an element with their roles that holds another interactive element (a link, a button, a form field, a focusable `tabindex`, or one of eight interactive roles), unless that element is hidden, inert or `aria-hidden`. axe's `nested-interactive` looks only inside roles whose children are presentational (a button, a tab, a checkbox), and a link's are not, so a button inside a card's link passed axe (see Mutations).
- **No prefetch on the DS page.** `next/link` prefetches each link in view in a production build, and the product pages come in M3, so each prefetch of `/us/products/…` answered 404 and failed the cell's console check (all 60 ProductCard cells, the first time). The cards take `prefetch`, and the stories pass `false`; a shop leaves it unset.
- **`dev-console-ds.spec.ts`** has `/design-system/{locale}/molecules/variant-selector` in the four locales (the plan said `dev-console.spec.ts`; since T27 the DS pages are in `dev-console-ds`), so VariantSelector's hydration is checked in `next dev`.
- **The CI gate:** a molecule is the DS's own (`node scripts/ci-gate.ts --files packages/ui/src/molecules/price-block.tsx` runs `design-system` only), and T32's change to `packages/ui/package.json` runs all three jobs.

### How a component task uses them

1. A card takes the `sizes` of the column it sits in (`(min-width: 768px) 25vw, 50vw` for a grid of four from 768 px), and `copy={{ card: messages.molecules.productCard, priceBlock: messages.molecules.priceBlock }}`.
2. A molecule that adds a control to a card puts it outside the title's link, as quick add does; the DS's nested check fails otherwise.
3. VariantSelector's `name` must be unique on the page (radios with one name are one group to the browser), so two selectors on one page take two names.

The plan's first mutation said a nested button fails axe's `nested-interactive`; it does not, which is why the nested check was added.

### Decisions the plan did not settle

1. **The title link is `block min-h-11`, and its `::after` is the hit area and the ring.** The `Link` atom's own ring is `ring-0` in a card, so the ring is drawn once, around the card.
2. **The overlay variant's panel is opaque `bg-background`,** not a tint over the picture, so every text pair is measured against one colour: title 19.9:1, `price` 19.8:1, `price-sale` 6.42:1, `price-original` 7.81:1, `muted-foreground` 4.95:1, white on `badge-sale` 4.77:1 and on `badge-new` 5.25:1, `destructive` 4.77:1 (from the token values).
3. **At most two badges,** in this order: sold out, sale, new, bestseller, then the product's own. `minimal` and `compact` keep only "Sold out". Badges are `rounded-xl` rather than the atom's `rounded-4xl`, so a long German label that wraps is not cut by the corners.
4. **The swatches on a card are display only:** discs in a named list, up to five; over five, four discs and "+N" (with "N more colors" hidden); an unavailable colour is struck through and its hidden name says so. Choosing a colour is VariantSelector's, on the product page.
5. **Quick add:** "Choose options" when the product has more than one variant (the action then takes the shopper to the product page; the DS passes the product's link); a sold-out product's button is disabled and says "Sold out"; while adding, the button is `aria-disabled` (Base UI's `focusableWhenDisabled`) and `type="button"`, so it submits nothing twice, even before hydration; "Added to cart" (hidden) and the error (visible) are in a `role="status"` region that is always there. The button's name is its text and a hidden ", {title}".
6. **The rating on a card** is the Rating atom named "{average} out of 5, {count} reviews"; the visible "(128)" is `aria-hidden` and wraps below the stars in a narrow column. A product with no reviews shows nothing.
7. **Low stock is not drawn on a card:** SBP calls it optional and the plan's card does not list it.
8. **RatingSummary's bars are `bg-primary` on `bg-muted`:** the amber `rating` colour on `muted` is 2.94:1, under WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1.
9. **A SizePill in VariantSelector wraps** (`rounded-3xl max-w-full wrap-anywhere`): a long German or Greek value becomes a rounded rectangle, and one line is still a stadium. A colour value with neither a hex nor an image is a SizePill.
10. **A chosen value that becomes unavailable stays chosen,** and says so in its name, rather than the selector changing the shopper's choice for them.
11. **`figure.credit` in the fixtures is the name alone** ("Shopblok Studio"); MediaFigure's copy adds "Photo: {credit}". `unavailable` and the rating label are in two copy blocks each, so every component's `copy` stands alone.

### Smaller observations

- **VariantSelector needs JavaScript for the keyboard:** Base UI renders the radios with `tabindex="-1"` on the server, so Tab and the arrows work after hydration; without it, only the first choice reaches a form.
- **The card's `href` is cast** to `Link`'s own `href` type in `parts.tsx`: the storefront's typed routes narrow it, and the card's link comes from data.
- **The Greek, German and French copy** of the new keys was drafted in this session, for W4's read.

### Review fixes (PR 54)

| Finding | Fix | Test |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Quick add sent only `productId` and `handle`, so M3's action could not tell an add from "choose options", nor which variant to add | the card contract has an optional `variantId` (the only variant's, when `variantCount` is 1); the form sends `intent=add` with `variantId`, or `intent=choose` and no variant id (several variants, or one without its id), and the button says "Choose options" then | `product-card-parts.test.tsx`: the submitted FormData for each case |
| 2. Badge keys `${kind}-${label}` repeat for two alike badges | keyed by place | two alike badges render with no console error |
| 3. `image-swap`'s second picture was only `opacity-0`, so every card in view downloaded it, on phones too | `hidden` by default, `block` only under `@media (hover: hover) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, so a lazy image that is never shown is never fetched; `swapped` still draws it | the classes for both, and `swapped` |
| 4. ReviewItem split paragraphs on `\n\n` only | a blank line in LF or CRLF, with spaces on it, ends a paragraph | a CRLF body with a spaced blank line |
| 5. The quick-add spinner was a `role="status"` Spinner inside the button | a bare `aria-hidden` loader icon (`data-slot=product-card-quick-add-spinner`); the visible "Adding…" is the name | the existing spinner tests on the new slot |
| 9 (optional). `nestedControls` counted any `[tabindex]` but `-1` and missed `summary` | `summary` is a control; a `tabindex` alone counts only when `tabIndex >= 0` | the DS run |

Findings 6 (one `MAX_STARS` and `{max}` in the card's rating copy), 7 (Image's ratio and radius tables exported for MediaFigure and the card) and 8 (one `SwatchDisc` shared with the Swatch atom) are optional refactors, left for a later tidy-up. **For W4:** Greek `quickAdd.chooseOptions` reads "choice of choices" ("Επιλέξτε παραλλαγή" or "Επιλογές" read better), and Greek uses both "κριτική" (RatingSummary) and "αξιολόγηση" (ProductCard) for a review.


## Discovery and site-wide molecules (T33)

**Result: SearchField, Breadcrumbs, Pagination, SortSelect, FilterGroup, ActiveFilterChips, EmptyState, MarketSwitcher, NewsletterForm, AccordionItem, Toast, CopyCodeChip and CountdownTimer are in `packages/ui/src/molecules/`, each with its registry entry, its story, its copy in the four catalogs, fixtures and tests; the `design-system` job opens MarketSwitcher and a toast from the keyboard at 375 and 1440 px and checks axe and focus on the open state (D45); a test reads the build's client chunks and finds no flag in them (D49); and the DS checks run on the fixtures' clock (D50).** The 13 new entries' 78 cells, the 4 interaction checks and the bundle test pass, and so do the 284 before them.

|---|---|
