### How it works

- **Discovery works without JavaScript (SPEC §8.4).** **SearchField** is a `<div role="search">` (the test tools do not know `<search>` yet) around a GET form: a labelled `type="search"` input named `q`, a clear button that appears once hydrated and there is text, and a submit button. **Pagination** is links only (a test finds no button in it), from `hrefFor(page)`: `aria-current="page"` on the current one ("Page 10 of 20"), previous and next left out at the ends rather than drawn dead, and an ellipsis; 7 slots from `sm` and 5 below, both windows in the markup with CSS showing one, so a crawler sees every link; nothing for one page. **SortSelect** is a GET form with a submit button that stays after hydration; a choice from the pointer or the open list submits, a key press on the closed select does not (WCAG 3.2.2), and `SortState.params` carries the filters as hidden inputs without the page, so a new sort starts at page 1. **Breadcrumbs** collapse the middle below `md` when two or more steps sit between Home and the parent; the ellipsis is text, not a disclosure, and the current page is text with `aria-current`. **EmptyState** is an icon, a title, a text and an action (a link with button classes); it has no words of its own.
- **Filters are one GET form's fields.** **FilterGroup** sends `{facet.id}={value}` for each chosen checkbox or swatch, `{id}.min` and `{id}.max` for a range, and `{id}=1` for a switch. Counts are drawn `aria-hidden` and read as a hidden ", N products". An option with no product is disabled unless it is chosen (a stale link's filter must come off). "Show more" is a native `<details>`, which opens by itself when a chosen option is inside it and still submits its closed fields. The price range is the slider primitive's two thumbs and two labelled number fields; an empty field means no limit, and a thumb at its end empties its field, so an untouched range posts `price.min=` and `price.max=` (the app drops empty values). **ActiveFilterChips** is a `ul` of Chips whose remove control is now a link (Chip's third variant, `removeHref` and `removeLabel`, with the button's box and ring), named "Remove Color: Black", and "Clear all" is named "Clear all filters".
- **MarketSwitcher keeps the flags on the server (D49).** `market-switcher.tsx` is a server component: it makes every word (country names in the page's language, each language in its own with i18n's new `languageName`) and one `<Flag>` per country, and hands strings and the rendered flags to `MarketSwitcherOverlay` (`market-switcher-client.tsx`), which imports neither i18n, nor `atoms/flag.tsx`, nor `country-flag-icons` (a test reads its imports). From `md` up it is a popover (`modal="trap-focus"`, so the page behind stays scrollable), below it a modal bottom sheet (SPEC §9.4); both triggers are in the markup and CSS hides one, so the server and the browser agree with no `matchMedia`. Both have a visible close button: Base UI's popover traps focus only with a `Close` part inside it. Each language is a link named "Language, Country", the current one marked by a check, inverted colours and `aria-current`. `form="popover"` or `"drawer"` draws one form alone, for the DS's open states. `isFlagCode` and `FlagCode` are in `atoms/flag-code.ts`, which imports only `country-flag-icons`' root module (`hasFlag`, no drawing), and Flag's fallback passes on its props (PR 43 review, items 10 and 12).
- **NewsletterForm** is an email field, the consent sentence with the privacy link inside it (one ICU message with a `{privacy}` slot), and a submit button, with `idle`, `sending`, `done` and `error` as a prop. While sending, the button is `aria-disabled` and `type="button"`, and a hidden disabled submit button comes first, so Enter cannot submit twice (HTML's implicit submission uses the first one). **CopyCodeChip** is the code and a copy button whose name does not change ("Copy code WELCOME10"); "Copied" is announced by a `role="status"` line that is always there, and when the clipboard is missing or refuses, the code is selected and a line says to copy it. **CountdownTimer (D50)** is a server part that formats the label and the end time and a client clock (`countdown-clock.tsx`) read with `useSyncExternalStore`: its server snapshot counts from the contract's `now`, never `Date.now()`, so the server and hydration agree; the browser then ticks on each whole second and stops at zero. The digits are `aria-hidden` in a `role="timer"` with `aria-live="off"`, a hidden sentence ("3 days, 4 hours, …", `Intl.NumberFormat` units and `Intl.ListFormat`) says the same, and a `role="status"` line says once that it ended (WCAG 4.1.3). It takes `timeZone` (default `UTC`) for the end time, so the server and the browser write the same text.
- **AccordionItem** is built from Base UI's accordion parts rather than the primitive's trigger, which fixes `<h3>`: `headingLevel` (3 unless given), a chevron that turns, and a panel that animates its height, with nothing moving under reduced motion. **Toast:** `showToast(manager, message, copy)` adds a toast to the `Toaster` in `Providers`, with its kind's word ("Success") drawn beside the icon (WCAG 1.4.1); `Toast` draws one static, for the DS. Every kind is announced politely, an error too: Base UI's `priority: "high"` puts `aria-hidden` on a focusable toast. An error stays until it is closed; a success or an information leaves after 5 s, or 10 s with an action, and Base UI pauses the timer on hover and focus (WCAG 2.2.1). The primitive's list is now a grid (icon, text and close on one row, the action under the text) so a long German label does not squeeze the words.
- **The interaction checks (D45)** are listed in `apps/storefront/src/design-system/interactions.ts`: for each entry, the trigger (one attribute selector), what opens, where focus goes (`inside` or `stays`) and whether it traps focus. `design-system.spec.ts` opens each on the entry's preview page (`/design-system/en/preview/{id}`, the live render alone) at 375 and 1440 px: Enter on the visible trigger (again until it opens, since a press before hydration does nothing), axe on the open state, then for `inside` focus in the popup, Tab and Shift+Tab as many times as the popup has stops plus two without leaving it, Escape, and focus back on the trigger; for `stays`, focus still on the trigger and a live region that says the toast. Base UI's focus guards (an `aria-hidden` element on each side) take focus first and hand it on a frame or two later, so the trap check waits up to a second for focus to come back before it counts a press as leaving. MarketSwitcher is checked at both widths, so both forms are; `stories.test.tsx` checks that each listed entry's live render draws its trigger.
- **The bundle test (D49):** after the build, "no client chunk holds a flag (D49)" reads every `.js` file under `.next/static` for the start of the longest path of each market's flag (from `country-flag-icons/string/3x2`), and expects Cyprus's and the United States' needles to be long enough to be their own.
- **The fixtures' clock (D50):** the DS cells and the interaction checks call `page.clock.setFixedTime(fixtureNow)` before they load the page. Without it, every countdown state reads "Ended" after hydration, since the fixtures' dates are behind the real clock.
- **The registry** lists 28 molecules (68 entries): the 13 above, after T32's 15. Each has a contract (`SearchQuery`, `Breadcrumbs`, `PageState`, `SortState`, `FacetGroup`, `ActiveFilters`, `EmptyStateContent`, `MarketChoice`, `NewsletterSignup`, `AccordionSection`, `ToastMessage`, `DiscountCode`, `Countdown`).
- **`dev-console-ds.spec.ts`** has `/design-system/{locale}/molecules/market-switcher` in the four locales and `/design-system/de/molecules/filter-group`, so the switcher's and the price range's hydration are checked in `next dev`.
- **The CI gate:** the molecules, the stories, the contracts and `interactions.ts` are the DS's own (`design-system` only); T33's changes to `packages/ui/package.json` and `primitives/toast.tsx` run all three jobs.

### How a component task uses them

1. The headers and footers pass MarketSwitcher a `MarketChoice` from the market resolver and leave `form` unset; `form` and `defaultOpen` are for the DS's states.
2. A listing page passes Pagination an `hrefFor` that keeps the filters and the sort, and SortSelect `params` with the filters and without the page; it drops empty `price.min` and `price.max`.
3. A new overlay (a dialog, the cart drawer, a menu) gets a line in `interactions.ts`, and its trigger a `data-slot`, and the job checks it.
4. A toast comes from `showToast(useToastManager(), message, copy)` in a client component (`useToastManager` is the toast primitive's); `copy` is `messages.molecules.toast`.

### Measured

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| The `design-system` project on `next start`, built with `DESIGN_SYSTEM_ENABLED=true` | **367 passed** in 5.8 min: the 284 before, the 13 new entries' 78 cells, the 4 interaction checks (MarketSwitcher and the toast at 375 and 1440) and the bundle test |
| The same, the first time | 361 passed, 6 failed: SearchField and SortSelect at `el` 375 (`scrollWidth 405, innerWidth 375`: a long submit label in a `shrink-0` button; now `max-w-full`, so it wraps), MarketSwitcher's popover states at 768 and 1440 (`scrollHeight 786 > clientHeight 718`: the box is now 880 px, not 720), and the sheet's interaction check at 375 (`Shift+Tab leaves the popup after 2 presses`: the focus guard, see above) |
| `dev-console-ds` in `next dev` | 21 passed in 2.2 min: MarketSwitcher in the four locales and FilterGroup in `de`, 0 console messages, 0 failed requests |
| `e2e-smoke`'s suites on `next start`, default build, `E2E_TEST_ROUTES=true` | 86 passed in 42.0 s |

### Mutations

Each applied, checked and reverted from a copy.

| Mutation | Check | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `Flag` imported in `market-switcher-client.tsx` and drawn in the trigger | the bundle test, after a flagged build | fails: `flags in client chunks`, `CY in .next/static/chunks/2flt1zz4n--j2.js` and the same for US, GB and CH: each market flag with a path of its own, in one chunk (`flag.tsx` imports the whole set, `import * as flags`) |
| The sheet without its trap (`Drawer modal={false}`) | the interaction check at 375 | fails: `Tab leaves the popup after 9 presses` |
| CountdownClock's server snapshot from `Date.now()` | `countdown-timer.test.tsx` | 4 tests fail, among them "counts from the contract's now, whatever the clock says" (the fixed-clock test) |
| The clock that never stops, `aria-live="off"` removed, the hidden first submit removed, the clipboard fallback not selecting the code, `timeZone` removed | the molecules' tests | each fails its test |

### Where it differs from the plan

1. **The interactions are a data module** (`interactions.ts`), not a field on the story: Playwright's loader cannot import the stories (D40's reason). A unit test ties each to its story.
2. **The trap check is added:** the plan's step 5 said focus in, Escape and focus back; the sheet's mutation above needs Tab and Shift+Tab to fail.
3. **The fixtures' clock is set now,** not in T40: CountdownTimer's states end after hydration without it.
4. **The hydration checks are in `dev-console-ds.spec.ts`,** where the DS pages have been since T27.

### Decisions the plan did not settle

1. **A zero-count filter option is disabled,** unless it is chosen; adding it can only give an empty page.
2. **Swatch filters are Base UI checkboxes drawn as the Swatch atom** (`role="checkbox"`, no `aria-pressed`), each named by a label beside it ("Black, 8 products"). Switches sit inside their label, with no fieldset.
3. **The price range's hidden inputs are 44 px** (`size-11!` and a translate in `filter-group-price-range.tsx`): Base UI draws them 14 × 14, under the DS's target size. The fix belongs in the slider primitive, which nothing else uses yet.
4. **On/off filters' chips say their label alone** (`ActiveFilter.group` is optional), with no "In stock: In stock".
5. **MarketSwitcher's popups take no focus when drawn open at first render** (`defaultOpen`, the DS's states): several on one page would take focus from each other, and Base UI closes a popup that focus leaves. Opened by a reader, they take it.
6. **The sheet's DS states switch off its slide-in and its overscroll bleed** (`[--bleed:0px] duration-0`), a band under its bottom edge that would stick out of the box; language names are capitalised, because `Intl` writes "français".
7. **The toast demo uses `timeout: 0`,** so the interaction check never races a timer.
8. **SortSelect's options come from the resolver,** which builds `SortState.options` from `molecules.sortSelect.options`; `SortState` rejects duplicate values and the sort's name inside `params`.
9. **Contrast relied on** (from the token values): `muted-foreground` on `background` 4.95:1 and on `muted` 4.54:1 (counts, unit names, descriptions), `destructive` 4.77:1, `success` 7.61:1, `input` and `ring` 3.03:1, `primary-foreground` on `primary` 20.12:1.

### Smaller observations

- **Base UI 1.9's accordion has no arrow keys,** so Tab moves between its triggers, and a closed panel is not in the markup: crawlers and readers without JavaScript see the questions only (`keepMounted` or `hiddenUntilFound` would change that; untested).
- **Before hydration** the copy button does nothing (the code is selectable text), the clear button is not there, and the slider's two thumbs are both named "Maximum price" (Base UI sets their names and values on mount).
- **The browser's own validation bubbles** (`required`, `type="email"`) speak the browser's language, not the page's.
- **happy-dom toggles a checkbox inside its label twice on Space,** so the tests press Space on the swatch, whose label sits beside it.
- **The Greek, German and French copy** of the new keys was drafted in this session, for W4's read.

### Review fixes (PR 55)

| Finding | Fix | Test |
|---|---|---|
| 1. NewsletterForm with no `action` submitted by GET, so the email went into the URL | `method="post"` unless the action is a function (React's) | `newsletter-form.test.tsx`: a form with no action posts |
| 2. SortSelect's `keyed` flag could stick when a key opened the native list (its keyup goes to the list), so later pointer choices stopped submitting | a pointer press clears the flag too | `sort-select.test.tsx`: Space, then a pointer choice, submits |
| 3. The DS's countdown states read "ended" once hydrated, because the browser counts from today and the fixtures' ends are in October 2026 | CountdownClock and CountdownTimer take `frozen`: the clock stays at the contract's `now` and never ticks; the DS passes it | `countdown-timer.test.tsx`: frozen a year later, the days state shows its digits and starts no timer |
| 4. CopyCodeChip said nothing on a second press with the same outcome | the status line is keyed by a press count, so it is written again and the live region says it again | `copy-code-chip.test.tsx`: a new node on the second press |
| 5. A toast's kind ("Error") was outside its name (Base UI names a toast by its title) | the toast is labelled by the kind and the title (`aria-labelledby`), only when there is a kind; otherwise Base UI's own name stands | `toast.test.tsx`: the dialog's name is "Error Added to cart", and the title alone without a kind |
| 6 (optional). The price slider's steps of 1 from a fractional `min` never reached `max`, so the far end sent a price and dropped the top items | the slider's ends are `Math.floor(min)` and `Math.ceil(max)` (the fields already clamp) | `filter-group-price-range.test.tsx`: 19.99 to 149.99, the far end sends no limit |
| 8 (optional). `buildFacets` ran twice per locale | built once; the active-filter chips use the sidebar's facets | the fixtures' tests |

Finding 7 (the collapsed breadcrumb steps below `md`) is the plan's design, left for W4. **For W4:** Greek `activeFilterChips.remove` reads better as "Αφαίρεση φίλτρου {filter}", and the Greek sort options are long for a native select on a phone.

### D48: where the address formats come from

The three packages the plan named, read from their published tarballs (`npm pack`, 2026-10-17):

| | `localized-address-format` 1.3.3 | `@piplup/libaddressinput` 0.2.7 | **`lib-address` 0.7.0 (chosen)** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Licence | MIT | Apache-2.0 | MIT |
| Field order | yes, in the local and the Latin script | yes | yes (`fmt`, `lfmt`) |
| Required fields | no | yes | yes (`require`) |
| Postal-code pattern and example | no | yes | yes (`zip`, `zipex`) |
| What a country calls its fields | no | yes, and English labels | yes (`zip_name_type`, `state_name_type`, `locality_name_type`); no labels |
| How the data is split | one module for every country (15 KB, 3.9 KB gzip) | one 2.65 MB chunk (398 KB gzip); by default it fetches Google's data service, which the cloud refuses | one JSON file per country: CY 135 B, US 9.2 KB (with its states), BR 697 KB (with its cities) |
| Unpacked | 101 KB | 8.6 MB | 2.1 MB |
| Dependencies | none | none | none |
| Published | 2025-10-23 | three versions on 2026-09-24 | 2025-10-09 |

Only `localized-address-format` lacks the required fields and the postal patterns, so the plan's fallback (our own table) was not needed. `lib-address` has Google's fields per country under MIT with nothing else attached; `@piplup/libaddressinput` has the same data plus code we do not use, in one chunk 20 times the size.

**How it is used:** `lib-address` is a pinned devDependency of `@shopblok/i18n`, not a dependency. `pnpm --filter @shopblok/i18n address-formats` (`packages/i18n/scripts/address-formats.ts`) reads its 252 country files and writes `packages/i18n/src/address-formats.json`: per country only what AddressForm uses (the formats, the required letters, the pattern, the first example, the language, the prefix, the three name types) and only where it differs from Google's defaults, one country a line: 19.7 KB, 2.9 KB gzip. A test compares the file with the package, so an upgrade of `lib-address` fails until the script has run. `addressFormat(country, language)` (`address-format.ts`) turns an entry into rows of Medusa's fields, and `addressLines(address, language)` prints an address in its country's order with its separators ("Brooklyn, NY 11215", "CH-8001 Zürich"). Both run on the server: AddressForm hands the browser the formats of the countries it offers (the region's), a few hundred bytes each (300 B for Cyprus, 351 B for the United States, 1.5 KB for the United Kingdom, its postcode pattern), never the 20 KB file.

**What `addressFormat` decides** (`address-format.test.ts`, 30 tests with `addressLines`'):
- **Rows:** a row per line of Google's format; `%N` is first and last name side by side, `%A` is two rows of its own (lines 1 and 2). `%D` (dependent locality) and `%X` (sorting code) are left out: Medusa's address has no field for them, and no country requires them (a test reads all 252). Literal text (`〒`, `CH-`) is the envelope's, not the form's; a prefix is returned as `postalCode.prefix`.
- **Required:** the name always (Medusa's contract), then the country's letters (`A`, `C`, `S`, `Z`; Google's default `AC`).
- **Script:** where Google has a Latin-script order (14 countries: Japan, China, Korea, Russia, …), a page in another language than the country's uses it; Japan on an English page is name, company, street, prefecture, postal code. Languages are compared by their base subtag (Hong Kong's `lang` is `zh-Hant`).
- **Postal pattern:** Google's, with every letter matching in either case (`<input pattern>` is case-sensitive and a reader types "ec1y 8sy"), compiled under the `v` flag the attribute uses. All 181 patterns compile, and each country's examples match in upper and lower case (a test).
- **A country Google does not list** gets the generic form (name, company, two street lines, city, province and postal code, the street and the city required) with `known: false`, never an error; a listed country without a format gets Google's default (no postal code).
- **Not kept:** the sub-regions (the US states, the Japanese prefectures). The province is a text field with `autocomplete="address-level1"`; a select of a country's regions is a later choice.

### How it works

- **The forms work without JavaScript (D48).** Every form here is a plain `<form>` whose values and errors are props, and every sending state is T33's: the button `aria-disabled` and `type="button"`, a hidden disabled submit button first (so Enter cannot submit twice), the fields read-only, and the words in a `role="status"` region that is always there. A string `action` posts (`method="post"`) and a function action is React's; ShippingEstimator and the remove confirmation's fallback without JavaScript are GET forms.
- **AddressForm** is a server component that formats everything (country names in the page's language, each country's rows, labels, required fields and postal hint) and a client part, `address-form-fields.tsx`, that imports no i18n and holds the chosen country and the typed values. The country select offers only `countries` (the region's, §8.4); the fields sit in one keyed grid in the country's order, so a field two countries share keeps its place, focus and text when the country changes, and a hidden status line says "The address fields now follow Germany". Without JavaScript the form shows the starting country's fields and submits whichever country is chosen; the server draws the right form again. Every field has its WCAG 1.3.5 token (`given-name`, `family-name`, `organization`, `address-line1`, `address-line2`, `address-level2`, `address-level1`, `postal-code`, `country`, `tel`), prefixed `shipping` or `billing` when `section` says so; phone is `type="tel"`. A required field has `required` and no mark; an optional one says "(optional)" in its label, and a note says the others are required (WCAG 3.3.2). The postal code gets the pattern, a `title` and a visible hint ("Enter a postal code like 2008"), a numeric keyboard when the country's codes are digits, and its prefix (`CH-`) as an `aria-hidden` addon. Errors (`required`, `pattern`, `invalid`) are text beside their field with `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`, and the status line counts them; they belong to the starting country and are dropped when another is chosen. **AddressCard** is an `<address>` of `addressLines`, the default marks as words, an edit link and a remove form, both named for the address ("Remove the address of Maria Georgiou, Nicosia", the visible word first, WCAG 2.5.3).
- **CartLineItem** is the picture (decoration, `alt=""`), the title (a link, clamped to two lines), the options (`Intl.ListFormat`), the unit and line prices, a stock warning, the quantity and a remove button, in two forms, so Enter in the quantity never presses remove. The quantity is the QuantityStepper atom in a client part (`cart-line-quantity.tsx`) that submits its form 500 ms after the last change, or at once on Enter (SBP `cart.md`: 300 to 500 ms), so three presses on "+" are one request; it shows the cart's quantity again when the cart's value changes or `pending` ends, so a refused change does not stay. Base UI's number field needs a script, so without one the stepper form is hidden (`noscript:hidden`, Tailwind's `@media (scripting: none)`) and a native number field with an "Update" button shows instead. The controls are named for the line ("Quantity, Linen shirt (Blue, M)"), so two lines of one product differ. A pending line is `aria-busy`, its controls inert, and says "Updating…". Its layout follows container queries (`@xs`, `@lg`), so it fits a drawer and a page column.
- **PromoCodeField** is a native `<details>` (it opens without JavaScript; the Collapsible primitive needs it), whose client part only keeps it open: applying a code does not close it under the focused button, and an error opens it. Applied codes are chips whose remove buttons are submits of one form (`name="code"`, the code as value): the Chip atom's remove is a link or an `onClick`, not a post. The errors are `invalid`, `expired`, `not-applicable`, `already-applied` and `failed`; while one code is applied, the others' remove buttons are inert too. **FreeShippingProgress** is a sentence in a polite status region ("Add €12.00 more for free shipping") and the Progress atom named by it; the bar never reads 100 before the threshold is met, and the reached state turns the truck into a check and the bar `success`.
- **ShippingOptionCard and PaymentMethodCard** share `radio-card.tsx` (internal, no entry): a `<label>` around an `sr-only` radio, so it works without JavaScript, the chosen state a 5 px ring on the mark (it survives forced colours) and a primary border, focus a ring on the whole card. The caller draws the group (`<fieldset>`, `<legend>`) and passes `name`. A price of 0 is the word "Free" in `success`, an unavailable option says "Not available for this order" (the contract has no reason), and a pickup option prints its address with `addressLines`. A method's marks are `aria-hidden`; a hidden "Accepts Visa, Mastercard, and American Express" joins the radio's description only when the method's name does not already say every brand.
- **SavedPaymentMethodCard** is brand, last four, expiry, holder and the default mark, formatted on the server; `now` is a prop and the component never reads the clock (expiry in UTC: a card works through its last month). The card's own width sets its layout (Remove beside the details from 24rem, the mark above them below 10rem), through an inner box, since a container cannot query itself. Remove opens a confirmation in a client part (`saved-payment-method-remove.tsx`): the Dialog primitive as an alert dialog, focus on Cancel, no dismissal by a click outside, Escape and Cancel returning focus to the trigger; the confirm button says "Removing…" while it works. Its two buttons sit side by side when the popup is 24rem wide inside, not from a viewport width, so they fit in a narrow popup. Without JavaScript, `confirmHref` makes the trigger a GET form to the caller's confirmation page; without it, nothing can be removed before hydration.
- **OrderSummaryRow** is a `<div>` of `<dt>` and `<dd>` for a `<dl>`: subtotal, discount, shipping, tax and total (emphasised). A discount is a positive amount in the contract (as Medusa's `discount_total`) and is drawn with U+2212, which a screen reader says "minus"; a shipping of 0 is "Free", and a missing shipping or tax is "Calculated at the next step".
- **Stepper** is a `nav` around an `ol` (`aria-current="step"` on the current step, a hidden ", completed" after a done one, "Step 2 of 3:" before the current one), built from the stepper primitive's parts. ReUI's stepper is a tab list (`role="tablist"`, buttons with `aria-controls`), which a checkout's progress is not; three small edits let the primitive be a list (each in its header, nothing changes for a user of none): `role` on the root with `aria-orientation` only on a tab list, `StepperNav` spreading its props, `StepperItem` taking `render`. Done steps with an `href` are links back. Below a container width (`@lg` for up to three steps, `@3xl` for more) only the current label is drawn and the others are circles with hidden names.
- **ShippingEstimator** is a GET form to `estimate.action` with the country and the postal code (no `pattern`: the country can change in the browser, and the server answers `error="postalCode"`), and the answer in a status region that is always there: the available options as a list, a sentence when nothing ships there, or an error line. **VerificationNotice** says where the mail went and offers a resend after `resendInSeconds`; the wait is T33's clock (`createClock` from `countdown-clock.tsx`) in `verification-resend.tsx`, whose server snapshot is the prop, so the server and hydration agree. The hint line is not live (no announcement each second); one polite "You can ask for a new link now." is added when the wait ends.
- **PaymentIcon (PR 43 review, item 14).** The plan asked for a cold Vitest start with the root `simple-icons` import and with per-icon data. Per-icon data was faster in all three interleaved pairs (below), so `atoms/payment-marks.ts` holds the eight brands' titles, colours and paths (11 KB, simple-icons 16.35.0, CC0), `payment-icon.tsx` draws them, and `simple-icons` is a devDependency of `@shopblok/ui` used only by `payment-marks.test.ts`, which checks that every entry equals the package's. `packages/ui/NOTICE.md` says so; the trademark paragraph stays.
- **Two changes to the DS checks.** axe now skips Base UI's focus guards (`[data-base-ui-focus-guard]`, `axeScan` in `design-system.spec.ts`): empty `aria-hidden` spans with `tabindex="0"` that hand focus on as soon as they get it, which axe cannot see (its own exemption reads the `onfocus` property). It reports them unless a visible `role="dialog"` makes it think a modal is open, which is why MarketSwitcher's open states passed and SavedPaymentMethodCard's alert dialog did not; any other focusable element under `aria-hidden` is still reported (a mutation below). And each cell now looks for **content that scrolls sideways in its box**: `overflow-y: auto` computes `overflow-x` to `auto` as well, so a dialog whose content is too wide scrolls instead of clipping, and the clipping check missed it (a table's container and a scroll area's viewport are left out, since they are there to scroll).
- **The interaction check (D45)** has a third entry in `interactions.ts`: SavedPaymentMethodCard's remove button opens `[data-slot="saved-payment-method-confirm"]`, focus goes in and stays in, and Escape brings it back, at 375 and 1440 px.
- **The registry** lists 40 molecules (80 entries): the 12 above, after T33's 28. Their contracts are `CartLine`, `PromoCodeEntry`, `FreeShipping`, `Address`, `AddressFormState`, `ShippingOption`, `PaymentMethod`, `SavedPaymentMethod`, `SummaryLine`, `StepperState`, `ShippingEstimate` and `VerificationRequest` (the last four new in `contracts/checkout.ts`). They gained refinements: `AddressFormState` refuses a country listed twice and a value's country outside `countries`; `FreeShipping` a threshold of 0 or less; `PromoCodeEntry` a code applied twice (in any case) and discounts in two currencies; `SummaryLine` a negative amount; `StepperState` a step listed twice and a `current` that is no step; `ShippingEstimate` a country outside `countries`, a country or an option listed twice.
- **Fixtures** gained `cartSamples` (an out-of-stock line, one at its limit, one with no picture, one with no options; free shipping empty, almost, reached and large; promo codes empty, applied, typed, two and long), `addressSamples` (GB, FR, JP and an unlisted country, `ic`, and a mistaken US form), `paymentSamples` (cards expired and expiring this month, from `fixtureNow`, D50) and `checkoutFlow` (summary rows, steps, the estimator's answers, the verification's waits, and step labels in four languages).
- **`dev-console-ds.spec.ts`** has AddressForm in the four locales, CartLineItem in `el`, SavedPaymentMethodCard in `fr` and VerificationNotice in `de`, so the client parts' hydration is checked in `next dev`.
- **The CI gate:** the molecules, the stories, the contracts and `interactions.ts` are the DS's own; T34 changes two `package.json` files and the lockfile, so its PR runs all three jobs, `windows-smoke` included.

### How a component task uses them

1. T39's cart drawer and cart page pass CartLineItem `updateAction` and `removeAction` (M3's server actions) and `pending` from the action's state; the checkout's order summary is a `<dl>` of OrderSummaryRows.
2. A checkout or account page passes AddressForm the region's countries and `section`, and maps the action's zod issues to `errors` (a kind per field); M3 must also decide what `Address.city` (required) holds for the seven countries Google gives no city field: AE, GI, JP, KY, MO, NR and SG.
3. ShippingOptionCards and PaymentMethodCards go in a `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`, all with one `name`; SavedPaymentMethodCard takes `now` from the request and, for readers without JavaScript, a `confirmHref`.
4. A page that shows a wait (VerificationNotice) or a card's expiry passes the server's time; nothing here reads `Date.now()` during the server render.

### Where it differs from the plan

1. **Stepper uses the primitive's parts in a list,** not ReUI's tab list (above); the plan said "ReUI's stepper, `aria-current="step"`", and the molecule has both.
2. **PromoCodeField's disclosure is a native `<details>`,** not the Collapsible primitive, so it opens without JavaScript.
3. **The quantity has a fallback form without JavaScript,** which the plan did not ask for: the stepper alone cannot post without a script.
4. **`simple-icons` moved to devDependencies,** with the per-icon data; the plan asked only to keep the faster import.
5. **The DS checks changed** (above): axe skips Base UI's focus guards, and a cell fails when content scrolls sideways in its box.
6. **The address data is a generated module** of `@shopblok/i18n` (the plan's second option), and AddressForm hands the browser the offered countries' formats, not one, so the country can change without a round trip.

### Decisions the plan did not settle

1. **The form follows Google's data where it surprises:** Cyprus's postal code is optional (`require` is the default `AC`), and seven countries have no city field (above).
2. **Names are always first and last,** in that order, in the form and the card; there is no family-name-first layout for `ja` or `hu`.
3. **The United Kingdom's `post_town` is "Town or city"** on an English page, not "Post town", which a US reader would not know; the other languages say their own word.
4. **No "set as default" checkboxes** in AddressForm; the card shows the default marks as words.
5. **A promo code's chips are drawn in the molecule,** not with the Chip atom, whose remove cannot post a form (a follow-up could give it one).
6. **An unavailable shipping option says one sentence** for every reason; a card's brand is said once, never twice.
7. **The remove confirmation is an alert dialog** with focus on Cancel and no click-outside dismissal.
8. **A discount is positive in the contract** and drawn with a minus; a missing shipping or tax is "Calculated at the next step", not 0.
9. **ShippingEstimator does not check the postal pattern in the browser;** the server does.
10. **Contrast relied on** (from the token values): `muted-foreground` on `background` 4.95:1 and on `muted` 4.54:1, `destructive` 4.77:1, `success` 7.61:1, `input` and `ring` on `background` 3.03:1, `primary-foreground` on `primary` 20.12:1, `secondary-foreground` on `secondary` 16.44:1.

### Smaller observations

- **Two rings are 2.78:1, under WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1:** an unchosen radio card's mark (`input`) on a hovered card (`muted`), and a promo chip's remove ring where it crosses the chip (`ring` over `secondary`, the Chip atom's own pairing). The mark's inner edge, against its own white fill, is 3.03:1, and the chip's 44 px ring lies mostly on the page. axe does not measure either; a darker `input` or `ring` token would fix both and is a design choice.
- **`primitives/stepper.tsx` changed** for the first time since T31 (three edits, above), and its header records them.
- **The browser's own validation bubbles** (`required`, the postal `pattern`) speak the browser's language; the `title` carries our hint.
- **If a reader types a quantity, presses Enter and the cart refuses it,** the posted value is the cart's again, but the field shows what was typed until it loses focus (Base UI does not rewrite text being typed).
- **Before hydration** the remove confirmation cannot open without `confirmHref`, and the resend's wait is the number at render time; a reload asks the server again.
- **The Greek, German and French copy** of the new keys was drafted in this session, for W4's read.

**CI fix (PR 56).** `check (Node 22)` failed two French cases in `molecules-cart.test.tsx` and `molecules-checkout.test.tsx`: the runner's Node 22 ICU writes fr-CH thousands with `'` (`1'234'567.89 CHF`; Node 22.22 here writes a narrow no-break space), and React escapes `'` in the markup as `&#x27;`, which the tests' `text()` did not decode. Both now decode entities, as `molecules-address.test.tsx` and `molecules-payment.test.tsx` already did. The cart test's `says` (and four lines like it) still escaped the expected sentence, so on the runner a decoded `'` met an expected `&#x27;`; text that has been decoded is now compared with the sentence as it is. The two AddressForm tests that render every country's form (3 to 6 s on the runner) have a 30 s timeout; one passed the 5 s default there.

### How it works

- **Server parts and client parts (D49).** Each organism is a server component that makes every word (`formatMessage` for "Shop all Women", "2 of 3", "Back to Menu", "Go to the Cyprus store", "{store}, home") and renders every flag, and a client part that takes plain data and nodes: it imports no formatter, no catalog and no flag, and a test in each file reads the client part's imports. The headers are server components too; the transparent one has a client frame of its own. CartButton, which the storefront's island renders in the browser, formats with the new `@shopblok/i18n/format` subpath (`formatMessage`, `formatNumber`), so its chunk does not take the four catalogs that the package's index exports.
- **AnnouncementBar** (SPEC §7.3) draws one message, or up to five in turn, each with an optional link that is a 44 px target of its own. With several it has a visible pause control that reads "Pause announcements" and then "Play announcements" (WCAG 2.2.2), previous and next (which pause too, so the chosen message stays), the position ("2 of 3", read ahead of each message) and a close button when the shop allows it. Rotation also stops while the pointer is over the bar or focus is inside it. A reader who prefers reduced motion gets a bar that starts paused and never moves on its own (read with `useSyncExternalStore`, server snapshot "no preference"); nothing is animated, a message is swapped. The messages are a live region that is `off` while the bar moves by itself and `polite` otherwise (the WAI-ARIA carousel pattern). Every message sits in one grid cell, the others `invisible`, `aria-hidden` and `inert`, so the bar is as tall as its longest message and does not jump; without JavaScript the first message shows and the controls are hidden (`noscript:hidden`). `rotateSeconds` below 5 counts as 5. Closing moves focus to the next control in the page (`focusAfter`, below) and then calls `onDismiss`.
- **MarketSuggestionBanner** is "Go to the Cyprus store" or "Stay in the United States store", from the `markets` global's suggestion (SPEC §7.3). It is per visitor, so the page passes it as `suggestion`, and without one, or for the country the page is already in, it draws nothing (D44). The sentence names the country with `Intl` and its currency, or is the shop's own message; the flag is drawn on the server and hidden from assistive technology. "Go" is an `<a hreflang>`, not next/link, because the whole page changes market; "Stay" is a button that hides the strip and moves focus on, hidden without JavaScript.
- **`focusAfter`** (`organisms/focus-after.ts`): when a control removes its own bar, focus goes to the first control after the bar in the page's order, where the next Tab would have gone, instead of `<body>`. Without one, the browser keeps its starting point.
- **MegaMenu** is one navigation landmark named "Main" whose items are links, dropdowns (a narrow panel under the trigger) and mega menus (a panel as wide as the root, with "Shop all Women" first, the columns as groups with their own "Shop all", and up to two featured tiles whose link covers the tile). It is built on T31's navigation-menu primitive. Base UI opens on hover and on Enter, Space and ArrowDown, keeps the panel open over the trigger or the panel, closes on Escape with focus on the trigger and lets Tab go from the trigger into the panel. One rule is ours: Base UI leaves a panel open when Tab from its last link lands on the next item of the bar, so the client part closes it when keyboard focus (`:focus-visible`) reaches another item. The panel's parts are laid out by their room (a grid of 11rem tracks, the tiles wrapping under the columns), so it is one column in a 375 px window; a mega menu's panel is as tall as the room the window leaves under the bar (`--available-height`) and scrolls inside it, and a dropdown never flips above its row, where it would cover the triggers. `splitAt` and `center` are the centered header's split navigation: one list, the logo a list item that is not a menu item between the halves, so the arrow keys cross from one half to the other and skip it (PR 57 review; `role="none"` on it failed axe's `list` rule). `panelClassName` reaches every panel's content (the DS's cap, below), and `defaultOpenItem` draws a panel open with no focus taken.
- **The navigation-menu primitive** gained, for the mega menu: the popup is a `div` (Base UI draws a second `<nav>`, which the trigger's `aria-owns` puts inside the root's landmark); `fullWidth` anchors the positioner to the root and makes the panel as wide as it, never flipping or shifting; `positionerClassName`, `popupClassName`, `sideOffset` and `collisionAvoidance` pass through `NavigationMenu`; and `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the positioner, the popup and the content. Its header lists the edits; its test covers the popup's element, both widths, the classes and reduced motion (`sideOffset` and `collisionAvoidance` need a layout, so the mega menu's cells check them).
- **MobileNavDrawer** is a 44 px menu button that opens a sheet from the start side (the sheet primitive, Base UI's Dialog: modal, focus trapped). The first level lists the items; a dropdown or a mega menu is a button that opens its level: a back button named for the level it returns to ("Back to Menu"), the label as a heading that takes focus, "Shop all …" and the links, a mega menu's columns as groups. Going back puts focus on the button that opened the level. The close button is the first control, in the flow. The first level's foot has the account links and the market switcher in its bottom-sheet form (`form="drawer"`). A link closes the sheet, it reopens at the first level, and nothing slides under reduced motion. The cart is never in the sheet (SPEC §9.4).
- **The six headers** (`header/parts.tsx` holds what they share). A variant returns the skip link ("Skip to content", to `#main` or `mainId`, hidden until focused, SPEC §13), then the announcement bar, then the `<header>`: the skip link is the first stop, and the bar is outside the header, so a sticky header (`sticky`) sticks alone and the bar scrolls away. Below `lg` (1024 px) every variant's row is a grid of the menu button, the logo in the middle and the search link and the cart at the end, and the drawer holds the navigation, the account and wishlist links and the switcher; from `lg` each variant has its own layout. Each piece is in the markup once and CSS places it, because the page holds one cart and the Tab order must follow what the eye sees (the centered header's logo is the one exception: two copies, one `display: none` at each width). From `lg` the logo takes at most 16rem in the four headers that put it beside the navigation, so a long store name wraps in its column instead of squeezing the navigation. The search is a link to the search page at every width (T37's overlay will open from it). Every control is 44 px, labels wrap and never truncate, and grid tracks shrink rather than widen the page.
  - **Classic:** one row: the logo, the navigation, the search, account and wishlist icons, the switcher (a popover from `md`) and the cart.
  - **Centered:** two rows from `lg`: the utilities and the cart at the end of a row above, and the navigation split around the logo (`splitAt` half the items) below, so the logo is centered on the page and the navigation has the header's width.
  - **Two-tier:** a utility bar above the main row, at every width, with the switcher at its start (popover from `md`, bottom sheet below) and, from `lg`, the account and wishlist as words; the main row is the logo, the navigation, the search and the cart.
  - **Mega menu:** two rows from `lg`: the logo, a wide search (the same link drawn as a field with the word "Search"), the utilities and the cart; then the navigation in a row of its own, so a panel spans the header's content.
  - **Minimal:** the menu button at every width, the logo in the middle, the search and the cart; the account links, the wishlist and the switcher are only in the drawer.
  - **Transparent:** the classic layout over the page's hero. The `<header>` has no height and its row is laid over what follows it; over the picture the text is light on a scrim (the `overlay` token under the row and a strip that fades out under it), with the tokens remapped inside the row so every component keeps its contrast pairing. It turns solid (the background token, a rule) once the page scrolls 8 px or a menu, the switcher or the drawer opens: a client frame reads the scroll with `useSyncExternalStore` (server snapshot "not scrolled") and watches `aria-expanded` in the header with a MutationObserver, so the organisms need no callback. `solid` pins the look.
- **The cart island (D44, step 4).** CartButton (`header/cart-button.tsx`) is a 44 px link with the bag icon, a hidden "Cart", a polite live region that is there from the first render and empty, and, when it has `count`, the region's words ("4 items", "empty") and a badge on the icon's corner, out of the flow, so nothing moves when the number arrives; above 99 the badge reads "99+" and the name keeps the number. It has no hook, so the header renders it on the server without a count, the placeholder every prerendered page holds. `apps/storefront/src/lib/visitor/` has the visitor store (`subscribe`, `getSnapshot`, `getServerSnapshot` returning "unknown", `setVisitor`, which ignores an unchanged count), `useVisitor` (`useSyncExternalStore`) and `VisitorCartButton`, the client component a page passes as the header's `cart`. Because the server snapshot is "unknown", the server render and hydration both draw the placeholder, and the count comes after. In the DS, `VisitorFixture` sets the fixtures' visitor (4 items) in an effect after hydration, as M3's answer will; never in a render, which also runs on the server, where the store is the process's.
- **The static check (step 5)** is in `design-system.spec.ts`: for each of the six headers (the `header` family; a test checks there are six) it fetches the entry's preview page as `curl` would and requires exactly one cart link whose HTML holds the empty live region, no badge and the text "Cart" alone; then it opens the page in Chromium and waits for the badge to read "4" and the link's name to be "Cart 4 items".
- **The DS checks run with reduced motion (D50):** the `design-system` project's context sets `reducedMotion: "reduce"`, so a rotating bar is paused in every cell. AnnouncementBar is the first entry that moves by itself.
- **The interaction check (D45)** has a third kind, `menu`, for a navigation panel, which is not a dialog: focus stays on the trigger when it opens, Tab goes into the panel, Escape closes it with focus back on the trigger, Enter opens it again and Tab past every stop of the panel closes it. `interactions.ts` has three new entries at 375 and 1440 px: MegaMenu (`menu`), MobileNavDrawer (`inside`, trapped) and the two-tier header's market switcher (`inside`, trapped).
- **States in a stack.** A story can set `statesLayout: "stack"` (`types.ts`, `entry-body.tsx`): its states take the frame's whole width, one under the other, because a bar or a header follows the window's breakpoints and not its card's. The navigation and header stories use it.
- **Open states in a box (D45), and a pitfall.** The open panels and sheets are drawn in OverlayBoxes with the organisms' own ways of starting open (`defaultOpenItem`, `defaultOpen`, `modal={false}`, the slide off), passed by the headers' `drawn` prop (for the DS only). Base UI sizes a panel by the room the *window* leaves (`--available-height`); for a box below the fold that is negative, `max-height` ignores it, and the panel runs out of its box. So the open states cap the panel (`panelClassName="max-h-[30rem]"`) and it scrolls inside the cap. A header's panel state is drawn from `lg` and its drawer state below it, each with a note at the other widths, so no sheet is drawn without its button; the minimal header's drawer is drawn at every width.
- **Landmarks in the DS.** One DS page holds a header per state, so each state's navigation and announcement region are named with the state's label ("Main (Long labels)"); a shop's page has one header and the catalog's names.
- **The registry** has two new groups: `organisms` (AnnouncementBar, MegaMenu, MobileNavDrawer and MarketSuggestionBanner, with the contracts `AnnouncementBar`, `Navigation`, `MobileNav` and `MarketSuggestion`) and `headers-footers` (the six headers, family `header`, each with its `variant`, sharing the `Header` contract), 90 entries in all. `AnnouncementBar` takes 1 to 5 messages and `rotateSeconds` from 5 to 20; `MarketSuggestion` refuses a suggested country that is the current one; `Header` refuses the switcher without the markets.
- **Fixtures** gained `header`: the store's navigation (New in, Women and Men as mega menus, Accessories as a dropdown, Sale), the markets, a cart of 4, the announcement bar with one, three and a long message, the suggestions with the copy's message and with the shop's, the hero picture, and `long.navItem`, a mega menu whose labels are the locale's longest strings.
- **`dev-console-ds.spec.ts`** has the mega menu header in the four locales (the page with the most client code: the navigation, the drawer, the switcher and the island) and AnnouncementBar in `el`.
- **The CI gate:** `apps/storefront/src/lib/visitor/` imports CartButton, so the organisms are now shared code (the gate follows the chain from outside the DS, PR 49), and T35 changes `packages/i18n/package.json`; its PR runs all three jobs, `windows-smoke` included (`node scripts/ci-gate.ts --files …`).

### How a component task uses them

1. M3's layout renders the variant the `header` global names with the request-independent props and `cart={<VisitorCartButton …/>}`, and feeds the store with `setVisitor` once the browser has the visitor (the cart route, after hydration); the page's main content has `id="main"` (or the header gets `mainId`).
2. M3 decides the suggestion from the request's country and passes MarketSuggestionBanner in a slot; a prerendered page passes none.
3. A client parent that remembers a closed announcement passes `onDismiss`.
4. T37's search overlay replaces the search link in `parts.tsx` (`HeaderSearch`, `HeaderWideSearch`).

### Where it differs from the plan

1. **The dev-console pages are in `dev-console-ds.spec.ts`,** where T27 moved the DS pages, not `dev-console.spec.ts`: the mega menu header in the four locales, and AnnouncementBar in `el`.
2. **The navigation-menu primitive changed** (above), and its header records the edits.
3. **CartButton has no entry of its own:** it is part of every header, and the headers' states show it empty and over 99.
4. **D50's reduced motion** was set in the `design-system` project here; the config did not have it before.
5. **The interaction check gained the `menu` kind,** because a navigation panel takes no focus when it opens, which neither `inside` nor `stays` describes.

### Decisions the plan did not settle

1. **The skip link is the header's,** first in the page, before the announcement bar, to `#main` by default.
2. **The announcement bar stops for hover and focus, and previous and next pause it;** a link the contract marks `external` stays in the same tab, because the bar's copy has no "opens in a new tab" note.
3. **A mega menu's panel is as wide as the header's row** (`data-slot="header-row"`, which the navigation-menu primitive's `fullWidthAnchor` names; PR 57 review), not only the navigation's column in it; a dropdown is narrow under its trigger. The panel closes 200 ms after the pointer leaves both.
4. **The drawer's foot (account links, switcher) is on its first level only,** and the sheet reopens there; a link closes it.
5. **The centered header has two rows from `lg`,** with the logo in the markup twice; **the minimal header keeps the search** beside the cart; **the transparent header turns solid** at 8 px of scroll and while anything in it is open.
6. **The cart's name is "Cart 4 items"** and "Cart empty" for none; the badge reads "99+" above 99 and nothing at 0.
7. **The suggestion's "Go" is a full page load** (`<a hreflang>`), and "Stay" only hides the strip; remembering it is the page's.
8. **The panels' links are not in the server's HTML** until a trigger opens them (Base UI mounts a panel when it opens; the drawer's levels likewise), so a crawler that does not run the page finds the bar's own links only. Base UI's `keepMounted` on the content would put every panel, hidden, in each page's HTML: tried, it adds the fixtures' 33 links and changes nothing on screen, but every page would carry the whole category tree, and 26 tests that find "the panel" by its slot would need the open one. It is left for M3, which builds the navigation from the category tree (SPEC §7.3) and can weigh the page's weight against the links.

### Smaller observations

- **At 1024 px the classic and transparent headers, with every utility, leave the navigation about 350 px,** so its items wrap to a second line (about 88 px tall); they are never cut. The switcher's full label takes the room; a compact trigger at `lg` is a design choice.
- **axe runs the WCAG rules only,** so `landmark-*` (best practice) is not checked; the DS names each state's landmarks apart anyway (above).
- **The transparent header's text on the scrim:** white on 60 % black is 5.7:1 over a white photograph (the `overlay` and `overlay-foreground` pair).
- **Under `noscript`** the bar shows its first message and no controls, the banner its link alone; the drawer and the panels need JavaScript to open (decision 8 above).
- **The Greek, German and French copy** of the new keys was drafted in this session, for W4's read; Greek, German and French put the country name after a colon, so no declension is needed.

## Footers and site organisms (T36)

**Result: the five footers of SPEC §9.4 (multi-column, newsletter-first, minimal, wordmark and two-tier) are in `packages/ui/src/organisms/footer/`, and CookieConsent and the loading skeletons in `packages/ui/src/organisms/`, each with its registry entry, its story, its copy in the four catalogs, fixtures and tests; the visitor's cookie choice is D44's second island (`VisitorCookieConsent`, with `consent` in the visitor store), and the `design-system` job now checks that the cookie banner is not in the prerendered HTML, that it appears once the page has hydrated with "reject all" drawn as "accept all" is, and opens CookieConsent's dialog and the two-tier footer's switcher from the keyboard.** The 7 new entries' 42 cells, the 4 new interaction checks and the 2 cookie banner checks pass, and so do the 514 before them.

### How it works

- **The `Footer` contract** (`contracts/footer.ts`, SPEC §7.3's footer global) is the store's name and home link, up to five columns of links, an optional newsletter, up to eight social profiles (one per network, each an `https` URL), up to six legal links, up to eight payment marks (each once), the market switcher and the copyright line. It refuses the switcher without the markets, as `Header` does. The eight networks are Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, Pinterest, X, Threads and Bluesky.
- **The five footers** are server components (`footer/parts.tsx` holds what they share), so every word is made on the server and no catalog, formatter or flag reaches a client chunk (D49); the only client code is what their molecules bring (the accordion's Base UI parts and MarketSwitcher). Each is a `<footer>` (the page's `contentinfo`) on `bg-muted`, with one `<nav>` named "Footer" for the columns and one named "Legal" for the legal links, each left out when it would be empty.
  - **Multi-column:** the logo, the columns and the newsletter as the last column from `lg` (under the columns below it); a bottom row with the social links, the switcher, the legal links, the payment marks and the copyright.
  - **Newsletter-first:** the newsletter in a band of its own at the top, wide enough that its field and button share a row, then the logo, the columns and the bottom row.
  - **Minimal:** one row: the copyright, the legal links, the social links and the switcher. It leaves out the columns, the newsletter, the payment marks and the logo, and says why in its file: a row has no room for a list of links or a form, eight marks would be its widest part, and the header above holds the logo (the copyright names the store).
  - **Wordmark:** the multi-column layout, then the store's name drawn as wide as the footer. The name is hidden from assistive technology (the logo link names the store) and sized in `cqw` inside an `@container` wrapper (an element cannot query itself); `wordmarkSize` estimates the name's width from its letters, fills 90 % of the width on one line and keeps between 8 and 22 `cqw`, so a long name wraps at its spaces.
  - **Two-tier:** a main tier (the logo and the social links on a row, the columns and the newsletter under them), then a bar under a rule with the legal links, the payment marks, the switcher (a popover from `md`, a bottom sheet below) and the copyright. Exactly one switcher trigger is visible at each width.
- **Columns collapse under `md` (the plan's step 1)** by being drawn twice, with CSS showing one: below 768 px each column is an AccordionItem, collapsed, and from `md` the columns stand side by side as a heading and a list. A collapsed accordion cannot become an open column with CSS alone (its button would say "collapsed" over a list on screen), so each width gets the structure that is true for it and the other is `display: none`. Every link is in the server's HTML at both widths: the side-by-side copy holds them all, and the accordion keeps its closed panels in the page (`keepMounted`).
- **Social links** are 44 px links with the network's mark (copied into `footer/social-marks.ts` from `simple-icons` 16.35.0, as T34's payment marks were, and compared with the package by `social-marks.test.ts`), named "Shopblok on Instagram" (`socialLink`; the brand's name is not translated). `NOTICE.md` names the eight marks.
- **Links that open another site** (`external`) open a new tab through the Link atom, which says "Opens in a new tab" (`newTab`) after the link's text.
- **CookieConsent** (SPEC §8.4) is a strip fixed to the bottom of the window with the shop's sentence or the copy's, the cookie policy link in it, and "accept all", "reject all" and "choose", which opens a dialog with the three categories. It is a client component as a whole (it takes `onChoose`, keeps state and formats a sentence with a link in it, with `@shopblok/i18n/format`).
  - **Per visitor (D44):** `choice` `undefined` (the server and the first render in the browser) draws nothing, `null` (a visitor who has not chosen) draws the banner, and a choice draws nothing. Without JavaScript the banner never appears, so nothing but necessary cookies is set.
  - **A region, not a dialog:** a `<section>` named "Cookie consent" that takes no focus when it appears and leaves the page behind it usable (a cookie wall is not consent), on the `--z-overlay` layer below the dialog's `--z-modal`, with padding that keeps clear of a phone's home indicator. It scrolls inside itself at 60 % of the window's height at most.
  - **Refusing is as easy as agreeing:** "accept all" and "reject all" are spread from one constant (`ANSWER` in `cookie-consent-parts.ts`: the default variant and size), side by side and in the same order at every width, in the banner and in the dialog; "choose" and the dialog's "save my choices" are the quieter outline buttons.
  - **The dialog** (`cookie-consent-dialog.tsx`, Base UI's Dialog, modal, focus trapped) has necessary checked and disabled with "Always on", and analytics and marketing off until the visitor turns them on (nothing is pre-ticked), then the policy link, then accept, reject and save. Escape and the close button return focus to "choose" and record nothing. An answer closes the dialog first and is delivered once the popup has left the page (`onOpenChangeComplete`), so focus never lands on the dialog's leftovers.
  - **After a choice** the banner goes and focus goes where the next Tab would have gone (`focusAfter`, T35).
  - **WCAG 2.4.11 (Focus Not Obscured):** while the banner is shown its height is reserved at the end of the page as `padding-block-end` and `scroll-padding-block-end` on `<html>` (`cookie-consent-reserve.ts`, measured again by a ResizeObserver), so a control the visitor tabs to is scrolled clear of the banner and the last links can scroll above it; the root's own values come back when the banner goes. Both are needed: scroll padding alone cannot add room after the last line, and padding alone does not help a link in the middle of the page.
- **The cookie island** (`apps/storefront/src/lib/visitor/cookie-consent.tsx`): `VisitorCookieConsent` reads the store with `useVisitor` and passes `undefined` for "unknown", the visitor's `consent` otherwise, and `setConsent` as `onChoose`. The store's `Visitor` gained `consent: ConsentChoice | null` (`ConsentChoice` is `{ analytics, marketing }`, strict); `setConsent` records a choice and does nothing while the store does not know the visitor, so every banner on the page goes at once. The choice lives for the page's life until a later milestone stores it in a cookie (M6 wires PostHog to it, SPEC §8.4). `VisitorFixture` takes `consent` (default `null`) beside `cartCount`.
- **The loading skeletons** are one entry (D46) with four layouts: a product grid (8 cards, in ProductCard standard's shape without a rating, in the grid T37's ProductGrid must keep), a product page, the cart (3 lines and the summary) and an account list (4 rows); `items` changes the count of all but the product page. Each is a `<section>` named for what loads ("Loading products") with `aria-busy="true"`, holding one `aria-hidden` box of Skeleton shapes: one named, busy region, and no live region, so nothing is announced. A server component; the pulse is the Skeleton atom's (`motion-safe:`).
- **The static check** is in `design-system.spec.ts` ("cookie consent · en · 375" and "· 1440"): it fetches CookieConsent's preview page as `curl` would and requires no banner and no accept button in the HTML, then opens it in Chromium, waits for the banner, compares what makes "reject all" and "accept all" prominent (height, background, text colour, border and type), and accepts, which must remove the banner.
- **The interaction check (D45)** has two new entries at 375 and 1440 px: CookieConsent's dialog, opened from "choose" (`inside`, trapped), and the two-tier footer's market switcher (`inside`, trapped). CookieConsent's is marked `afterHydration` in `interactions.ts`: its trigger is drawn only once the island knows the visitor, so `stories.test.tsx` checks that the server's markup has none of it, where for the other entries it checks that the live render draws the trigger.
- **Stories.** The footers' states (`statesLayout: "stack"`): the bare footer (passed whole: spread over the full one it would keep the newsletter and the markets), no newsletter, long labels, five columns, all eight networks and a column open (drawn under `md`, with a note from 768 px), and for the two-tier footer the switcher open as a popover (in a 1040 px OverlayBox) and as a sheet (720 px), with the footer reduced to its logo and bar so the popup has room under its trigger. The minimal footer has the bare, long and all-networks states only: it never draws a newsletter or columns. CookieConsent's live render is the real island in an OverlayBox with `VisitorFixture`, so its banner appears after hydration; its states (the banner, the shop's own sentence, the dialog, the dialog with analytics on) give the organism `choice={null}` and do not share the store. Every banner, region and footer landmark is named apart with its state's label, as the headers' are.
- **The registry** has 97 entries: `organisms` gained CookieConsent and loading skeletons (contracts `CookieConsent` and `LoadingSkeleton`), and `headers-footers` the five footers (family `footer`, sharing the `Footer` contract), so 21 entries have a family (D46's ProductCard 10, Header 6 and Footer 5).
- **Fixtures** gained `footer` (`content`: three columns, the newsletter, five profiles, four legal links, the eight payment marks, the markets and a copyright with the fixtures' year; `bare`: two legal links and the copyright) and `site.cookieConsent` (the policy link, the shop's own sentence in each locale, and the three choices a visitor can have made). The copy files gained the copyright line and the shop's cookie sentence.
- **`dev-console-ds.spec.ts`** has the two-tier footer in the four locales and CookieConsent in `de`.
- **The CI gate:** T36 changes code outside the DS (`lib/visitor/`) and no dependency file, so its PR runs `e2e-smoke` and `design-system` and skips `windows-smoke` (`node scripts/ci-gate.ts --files …`).

### How a component task uses them

1. M3's layout renders the variant the `footer` global names with its props, and `<VisitorCookieConsent policyHref=… />` once per page, after the main content; it feeds the store with `setVisitor` (the visitor's `consent` from the cookie, `null` when there is none).
2. M6 stores the choice in a cookie the browser can read, and loads PostHog only when `consent.analytics` is true (SPEC §8.4). It also decides how a visitor changes their mind: once they have chosen the organism draws nothing, and `defaultSwitches` sets the dialog's switches to a choice already made. **M6 must add a control that reopens the consent dialog** (for example a store action `reopenConsent()` that CookieConsent reads as "draw the banner with the dialog open, the switches from `defaultSwitches`", and a footer link "Cookie settings" that calls it): withdrawing consent must be as easy as giving it (GDPR Art. 7(3)). Until then the footer links only the cookie policy and the dialog promises nothing about changing the choice later (PR 58 review).
3. A route's `loading.tsx` renders `<LoadingSkeleton layout=… />`; T37's ProductGrid keeps the columns and gaps of the skeleton's `GRID` constant, and the skeleton changes with it if it does not.

### Where it differs from the plan

1. **The visitor's choice is a prop with an island,** as the cart's count is (T35), not a slot: CookieConsent takes `choice` and `onChoose`, and `VisitorCookieConsent` passes the store's. A slot would have put the same island one level up.
2. **The loading skeletons have a fifth state,** the product grid with three cards (`items`), beside the plan's four layouts.
3. **The dev-console pages are in `dev-console-ds.spec.ts`** (T27), as in T35.
4. **The interaction check gained `afterHydration`,** for a trigger the server's HTML cannot hold.

### Decisions the plan did not settle

1. **The minimal footer has no columns, newsletter, payment marks or logo** (above), and the minimal footer's social heading is for screen readers only.
2. **The footers' social profiles are eight networks** (above), each an `https` URL, with the marks of `simple-icons`.
3. **The banner's order is accept, reject, choose,** and the dialog's accept, reject, save, so accept and reject are side by side and in the same order in both.
4. **Analytics and marketing start off** in the dialog, and "save my choices" with nothing changed records a rejection.
5. **The banner is named by the catalog's `region`,** not by its heading, so the DS can name each state's region apart.
6. **The banner reserves its height on the root element** (2.4.11, above) rather than leave the page's end under it.
7. **The choice lives in the store for the page's life** until M6 stores it.

### Smaller observations

- **The Switch atom's hit area is 42 px, not 44** (its `::after` inset ignores the 1 px border), and an `id` passed to it lands on the hidden `<input>`, so a `for` label never names the `role="switch"` element. The dialog puts a Label around each switch, which the DS's 44 px check accepts (`closest("label")`); a later molecule that puts a Switch beside a `for` label will fail that check.
- **The CookieConsent page in the DS ends with up to 377 px of blank space** at 375 px: the reservation is the organism's own and runs for the banners in boxes too.
- **`keepMounted`, not Base UI's `hiddenUntilFound`,** for the footer's closed columns: once a script asks for a link's box, Chrome lays out the content an `until-found` panel skips, and the panel's `overflow-hidden` then reports clipping on every closed column. The cost: find-in-page does not open a closed column under `md`.
- **Short text links are narrower than 44 px** ("FAQ" was 29 px), so the footer's text links are `min-h-11 min-w-11`.
- **The storefront's island test runs in happy-dom** (`// @vitest-environment happy-dom`), which Vitest resolves as its own peer (20.14.5, pinned in the lockfile); the app does not list it, and adding it would change a dependency file and run `windows-smoke`. happy-dom answers a click that reaches a label from inside it with a second click on the control, so the test toggles a switch through its label (Chromium toggles once either way).
- **`@shopblok/ui` exports `organisms/*` as `.tsx` only,** so `footer/social-marks.ts` cannot be imported from the storefront.
- **The skeleton's card matches ProductCard standard without a rating;** a card with one is 22 px taller, which the skeleton does not reserve.
- **The Greek, German and French copy** of the new keys was drafted in this session, for W4's read.
