## next-intl (T46)

**Result: next-intl 4.14.9 reads the request's market from the `[market]` root param (D62), and `pnpm build` passes with it, with and without the stack.** The wiring page, the 404 page, the error state and the layout's toast copy come from `getTranslations`; the client provider gets two messages and no catalog; a market in a language with no catalog (Mongolian) shows English text with its own `lang` and its own number format. `curl` of `/`, `/us`, `/gb`, `/de`, `/fr`, `/ch` and `/ch/fr` shows the same text as on `main`. The first-load JavaScript of `[market]` is 51 KB smaller than before, because `error.tsx` no longer carries the four catalogs. **The wiring page cannot carry `ensureStatic`** (it reads Medusa behind `connection()`), so the check was a probe page that used next-intl under `ensureStatic = "navigation"`: it built, and the two changes that make next-intl read the clock or the request were each refused by the build (below). The probe is not in the repo; the first page that stays static, T51's home, carries the export for good.

| | |
|---|---|
| Date | 2026-10-25 |
| Branch | `m3/t46`, from `main` at `0bcd634` |
| New | `apps/storefront/src/i18n/{request,messages,app-config.d}.ts` and the tests of the first two; `src/app/(storefront)/[market]/{layout,page,error,not-found}.test.tsx`; `e2e/i18n-messages.spec.ts`, `e2e/support/catalogs.ts` |
| Changed | `apps/storefront/{package.json,next.config.ts,vitest.config.ts}`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (`allowBuilds`), `src/app/(storefront)/[market]/{layout,page,error,not-found}.tsx`, `src/lib/{market-locale,current-market}.ts` and `market-locale.test.ts`, `src/next-config.test.ts`, `e2e/wiring.spec.ts`, `packages/i18n/src/messages.test.ts` |

### How it works

- **The plugin.** `next.config.ts` wraps what `withPayload` returns in `createNextIntlPlugin("./src/i18n/request.ts")`. Under Turbopack the plugin's only job is an alias, `next-intl/config` → that file, and the path has to be relative to the app (an absolute one is refused); `next-config.test.ts` checks the alias and that the monorepo root, Cache Components and the DS flag survive the wrapper. Nothing of next-intl's routing is used: no middleware, no `Link`, no `createNavigation` (SPEC §8.5).
- **`src/i18n/request.ts`** is one `getRequestConfig` that ignores its arguments: `getCurrentMarket()` (the `market` root param, the cached map from `getRenderMarketMap()`, a 404 for an unknown key, `withLocale`'s English fallback) gives `locale: market.htmlLang`, `timeZone: market.timeZone` and `messages: catalogs[market.locale]`. It must not read `requestLocale`: next-intl's `requestLocale` is a getter that calls `headers()` the first time anyone reads it (`getRequestLocale` in `next-intl/dist/.../RequestLocale.js`), and a page that reads headers is dynamic, which `ensureStatic` refuses. `request.test.ts` hands the config a `requestLocale` that throws when read.
- **One fallback rule.** The catalog is `catalogs[market.locale]`, where `locale` is `withLocale`'s: the market's language when `@shopblok/i18n` has a catalog for it, English otherwise. `catalogs[market.language]` would be a second rule, and `catalogs["mn"]` is `undefined`: next-intl then prints the key (`notFound.title`) in the page, which is how the first mutation below shows. `locale` is the lang value, so `Intl` writes numbers, dates and money for the market's country in a language that has no catalog (`₮ 12,000.00` in `mn`, `MNT 12,000.00` in `en`).
- **A fifth language** is one entry in `LOCALES`, its module in `packages/i18n/src/messages/`, a line in `catalogs`, and a market whose language is that code. Nothing in `src/i18n/` changes.
- **The time zone.** `CurrentMarket` has `timeZone`, and `withLocale` sets it to `DEFAULT_TIME_ZONE`, `"UTC"`, until D65 gives each country its zone. Without one next-intl falls back to the zone of the machine that renders, so a prerender on a build machine and a browser would write different times (and next-intl calls `onError` with `ENVIRONMENT_FALLBACK` when it formats a date).
- **What a client island gets.** `NextIntlClientProvider` given no `messages` sends the whole catalog to the browser, on the server as well as in a nested provider (`NextIntlClientProviderServer` fills in `await getMessages()`). `src/i18n/messages.ts` has `pick(messages, paths)`: a path names a message or a namespace (`"molecules.cartLineItem"`), typed as `MessagePath` from the English shape, so a typo is a compile error; the result is a copy (a client component never holds the catalog's own object); a path that holds nothing throws. A nested provider's `messages` **replace** its parent's (use-intl's `IntlProvider` keeps the parent's only when it is given none), so a page's provider lists what its islands need and nothing more.
- **The layout.** `[market]/layout.tsx` reads the toast copy with `getTranslations("primitives.toast")` and wraps `Providers` in `<NextIntlClientProvider messages={pickShell(messages, market.locale)}>` (`pick(messages, SHELL_MESSAGES)` with the English catalog as the fallback; "Review fixes (PR 70)", item 2). `SHELL_MESSAGES` is, today, the error state's two lines (`wiring.backendUnavailable`, `wiring.backendHint`); T48 adds the header's and the cookie banner's namespaces when it builds them. `<html lang>` is still `market.htmlLang`.
- **The pages.** `page.tsx` and `not-found.tsx` call `getTranslations("wiring")` and `getTranslations("notFound")`; prices still go through `formatMoney(…, market.htmlLang)`. A page task passes a component its `copy` object from `(await getMessages()).molecules.cartLineItem` (the whole catalog is on the server only) and a single string from `t(…)`; a file that a client component imports must not import `catalogs`. `error.tsx` is a client component: it used to read `catalogs` by the language in the URL (all four catalogs in every page's JavaScript, below) and now calls `useTranslations("wiring")`, inside the layout's provider. `global-not-found.tsx` renders outside `[market]`, has no market, and keeps `catalogs.en`.
- **Types.** `src/i18n/app-config.d.ts` declares next-intl's `AppConfig` with `Messages` = the English shape, so `getTranslations("wiring")` and `t("title")` take only keys that exist. `Locale` stays a string: the lang value is `el-CY` or `mn`, which no closed list names.
- **The tests render the real thing.** In Vitest `next-intl/server` resolves to stubs that throw (its `react-server` export condition is not set), so `vitest.config.ts` aliases `next-intl/server` to the server build and `next-intl/config` to `src/i18n/request.ts`, which is what Next and the plugin do, and inlines `next-intl` and `use-intl` so the alias reaches the imports inside them. `page.test.tsx`, `layout.test.tsx` and `not-found.test.tsx` then run the real `getTranslations` through the real `request.ts` and `getCurrentMarket` with only `next/root-params` and the market map replaced, and render with `prerender` from `react-dom/static`, which waits for async components. A call to `headers()` outside a request would throw, so these also prove that the chain reads none.

### What the build said under `ensureStatic`

The wiring page's `MarketData` calls `connection()` and reads Medusa, so it is dynamic by design (it shows the backend's state live, and its error state is what the Medusa-down check above exercises); `export const ensureStatic = "navigation"` on it fails the build (last row). So the layout's next-intl calls were checked with a probe: `[market]/ensure-probe/page.tsx` with `ensureStatic = "navigation"`, a `generateMetadata` that calls `getTranslations("wiring")`, and a body that calls `getTranslations`, `getLocale`, `getFormatter` (`number` and `dateTime` of a fixed date), `getTimeZone` and `getMessages`, then a nested `<NextIntlClientProvider messages={pick(messages, ["wiring.market"])}>` around a client island that calls `useTranslations`, `useFormatter` and `useLocale`. Built with the stack, then deleted.

| Probe | What the build said |
|---|---|
| The page as above | **Passes** (`✓ Generating static pages … (38/38)`); `/el-cy/ensure-probe` and `/en-us/ensure-probe` are `○` (static), and `.next/server/app/el-cy/ensure-probe.html` holds `lang="el-CY"`, `<title>Έλεγχος σύνδεσης Shopblok</title>`, `UTC`, `1.234,50 €`, `1 Ιαν 1970` and the island's text, rendered at build time |
| The page also calls `getNow()` (and `format.relativeTime(date, now)`) | **Fails:** `Error: Route "/[market]/ensure-probe": Next.js encountered the unstable value \`new Date()\` while prerendering. This value can change between renders, so it must be either prerendered or computed later.` (`getNow` at `page.tsx:22`; `blocking-prerender-current-time`). It is Cache Components' rule, not `ensureStatic`'s: a page without `ensureStatic` would stream it. Pass `now` yourself, or leave relative times to a client island |
| `request.ts` reads `requestLocale` (`async ({ requestLocale }) => { await requestLocale; … }`) | **Fails**, twice: `Next.js encountered uncached or runtime data in \`generateMetadata()\` on a route that must be fully static.` (`static-metadata-dynamic`) and `Next.js encountered uncached or runtime data on a route that must be fully static.` (`static-route-dynamic`) |
| The same change on the repo as committed (no probe, no `ensureStatic` anywhere) | **Fails too:** `Error: Route "/[market]": Next.js encountered uncached or runtime data during prerendering. \`fetch(...)\`, \`cookies()\`, \`headers()\`, \`params\`, \`searchParams\`, or \`connection()\` accessed outside of \`<Suspense>\` prevents the route from being prerendered` (`blocking-prerender-dynamic`), on `/en-us`: the layout awaits the config above every `Suspense`. So Cache Components alone refuses a config that reads the request; `ensureStatic` is the net for a page that sits under its own `Suspense`. In Vitest the same change fails 20 tests in 4 files (`Error: \`headers\` was called outside a request scope`) |
| `ensureStatic = "navigation"` on the wiring page itself | **Fails:** `Error: Route "/[market]": Next.js encountered uncached or runtime data on a route that must be fully static.` with the `Suspense` that wraps `MarketData` in the stack |

So `ensureStatic` did complain, in the cases above and not in the one that matters: next-intl's calls and the root param are static-safe. It is placed on **no page in this PR**; T51's home and T49's product page are the first that can carry it (D58). The guards against a change that makes the config read the request are the build itself (the layout awaits the config, so `blocking-prerender-dynamic` fires, fourth row above) and, in Vitest, `request.test.ts` (a `requestLocale` that throws) and the layout, page and 404 tests (`headers()` outside a request scope throws): the mutation above fails 20 of them.

### Where it differs from the plan

1. **The probe, not a page, carries `ensureStatic`.** The plan's step 4 expected the build to pass "with `getTranslations` in the root layout and the wiring page" and asked where `ensureStatic` was placed. The wiring page cannot take it; the layout must stay `auto` (D58's step 1: it is above the dynamic cart and checkout). Section above.
2. **The chunk test reads the document as well as the scripts.** The plan wrote "the client chunks of `/` hold the picked namespaces only". A provider's `messages` prop travels in the RSC payload inside the HTML, not in a chunk, so a test of the chunk files alone would pass the provider that sends everything (the third mutation). `i18n-messages.spec.ts` reads the document and every script the browser loads.
3. **`error.tsx` changed,** which the plan did not list. It was the one place that put the catalogs into the client chunks, so the plan's own Verify ("the client chunks hold the picked namespaces only") could not pass without it.
4. **The shell's namespaces are the error state's two lines,** not "the header's and the consent's": they are built in T48, and a list of messages for components that do not exist yet would ship text nothing reads.
5. **`timeZone` lives in `market-locale.ts`,** beside the locale fallback (`withLocale`), not in `current-market.ts`: the pure, tested module holds both rules. `current-market.ts` only says that next-intl reads it.
6. **Mongolia's lang value is `mn-MN`,** unless its language row overrides it. The plan's test wanted `lang="mn"`; `request.test.ts`, `layout.test.tsx` and `page.test.tsx` cover the default and a row with `htmlLang: "mn"`.
7. **`@parcel/watcher` in `allowBuilds`** and the Vitest aliases are outside the plan's "Touches" list; both are needed (above).

### Decisions the plan did not settle

1. **`pick` takes typed paths and copies,** and throws for a path that holds nothing (item 1 of the mutations). A silent miss would ship an island with no text. The layout does not use that throw: it reads `pickShell`, which supplies the English message and warns ("Review fixes (PR 70)", item 2).
2. **`AppConfig` carries `Messages` only.** The typed `Locale` would need a closed list; the lang value is open.
3. **No `formats`, `now`, `onError` or `getMessageFallback`** in the config. A missing message shows its key and logs next-intl's `MISSING_MESSAGE`; the parity test in `packages/i18n` is what keeps a catalog complete, and M4's `ui-strings` loader is the place to decide a runtime fallback. `onError` and `getMessageFallback` are not inherited by client components (next-intl's docs): a client provider would have to define them.
4. **`global-not-found.tsx` stays on `catalogs.en`.** It renders for URLs no route handles, outside `[market]`, so it has no market and no root param.
5. **No layout test for a nested provider.** The page tasks add theirs, and each lists what its islands need.

### Smaller observations

- **Playwright's loader cannot import `@shopblok/i18n`:** the index imports `address-formats.json`, and Node's loader wants `with { type: "json" }` for it. `e2e/support/catalogs.ts` takes the four catalog modules directly (they import nothing at run time).
- **A missing message is a visible key,** not an error in the page: `notFound.title` in an `<h1>`.
- **next-intl checks the locale in development only,** with `new Intl.Locale(locale)`, and logs `An invalid locale was provided` instead of throwing; `mn`, `mn-MN`, `pt-BR` and `el-CY` pass.
- **`getNow()` and `format.relativeTime(date)` without a `now` break a static prerender** (above). `NextIntlClientProvider` does not set `now` by default for that reason.
- **`next/root-params` in Vitest** is a module the tests replace (`vi.mock("next/root-params", …)`), as `gate.test.ts` does; `next-intl/config`, a Turbopack alias, is replaced by the Vitest alias.
- **The Toaster's region label is not in the server HTML,** so the layout test reads the `copy` prop `Providers` receives, not the markup.

### Proof

`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` green at the root; `pnpm build --force` green with the stack and with no `.env`; `markets`, `wiring` and `i18n-messages` (55) on `next start` and `dev-console` (8) on `next dev`; both servers stopped by PID, ports 8000 and 9000 free, and `git status` clean. **Left for CI** (the PR changes `apps/storefront/**`, `package.json` and the lockfile, so the gate runs `check`, `backend-integration`, `e2e-smoke`, `design-system` and `windows-smoke`): `e2e-smoke`'s whole Playwright run (`payload-admin`, `payload-cache` and `payload-locales` also, which log in to or save the shared Payload database and so were not run on the shared machine); `design-system` (the DS pages are another root and do not call next-intl; expect no changed baseline); and `windows-smoke` (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` on Windows with `@parcel/watcher` set to `false`: its `win32-x64` binary comes with the platform package). To check: the PR's Checks tab; a failure in `i18n-messages.spec.ts` in `e2e-smoke` names the key and the URL it was found at.

### CI fix (PR 70)

The first run of PR 70 failed `design-system` at its build, in one second: `⨯ Failed to load next.config.ts` with `Error: Failed to load native binding`, whose cause was `Error: SWC native addon: validate cache root /github/home/.cache: cache root has a parent writable by another user without trusted sticky protection` (`ERR_SWC_NATIVE_CACHE`). The require stack runs from `next.config.compiled.js` through `next-intl/dist/cjs/development/plugin.cjs` to `@swc/core`: next-intl's plugin loads SWC with the config, which nothing did before T46. `@swc/core-linux-x64-gnu` 1.16.13 is a compressed carrier that unpacks the real addon into a cache, by default `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` or `$HOME/.cache`, and refuses a cache whose parent others can write without the sticky bit; in the Playwright container `HOME` is `/github/home`, so the job that runs there could not load it. `e2e-smoke`, `check` and `windows-smoke` run on the runner itself, whose `HOME` is fine.

Reproduced in the cloud VM with `HOME` under a mode-777 folder: `require('@swc/core')` fails with the same message. `SWC_NATIVE_BINDING_CACHE=0` (the README's "temporary materialization") fails the same way; `SWC_NATIVE_BINDING_CACHE=/tmp/swc-native-cache` loads it (`/tmp` is sticky; SWC creates the folder with mode 0700). So `design-system` and `update-baselines`, the two jobs in the container, set that variable at job level. A local machine needs nothing: a user's own `~/.cache` passes the check.

## Search on Postgres (T43)

**Result: the `product` index is ADR 0002's A′ (D63), and the S2 suite, ported for it, passes in `backend-integration`.** One searchable `search_text` holds every store locale's texts, the facets are ids, the three `translation.*` events re-index, and a middleware on `POST /store/search` gives the index the request's locale, checked against the store's. On the dev stack with the demo catalog, `κούπα` with `x-medusa-locale: el-GR` and `mug` with `en-US` both find `demo-ceramic-mug`, and the `category_ids` facet answers with its count; an edit of the mug's German title through the Admin API (`POST /admin/translations/batch`) made the new word searchable within a second, with no restart, and the edit back removed it.

| | |
|---|---|
| Date | 2026-10-26 |
| Branch | `claude/project-thread-lo9oew`, from `main` at `ad37f66` (PR 70 merged) |
| New | `apps/backend/src/search/helpers/{translations,facets}.ts`, `src/api/store/search/locale.ts`, `src/config/__tests__/search-{translations,locale-middleware}.unit.spec.ts`, `integration-tests/http/search-locale.{spec,fixtures}.ts` |
| Changed | `apps/backend/src/search/product.ts`, `src/search/helpers/resolve-product-ids.ts` (collections), `src/api/middlewares.ts`, `integration-tests/http/search-locale-assumptions.spec.ts` |

### How it works

- **Fields.** `search_text` (`text`, searchable with weight 2, never returned), `title` (the default language's: searchable with weight 3 as before, sortable and returned), `category_ids`, `collection_ids`, `tag_ids` and `option_value_ids` (`keyword` arrays, filterable, facetable, returned). `category` (names), `option_values` (`"Size:S"`) and `labels` (tag values) stay on the hits in the default language and are no longer facets or searchable; `description` left the index (it is in `search_text`). The status, the sales channels and the price fields are unchanged. The schema changed, so an existing database needs `medusa db:migrate` and a start (below).
- **The transform** (`helpers/translations.ts`, shared by `seed` and `consume`): `storeLocales` reads the store's `supported_locales` once per batch, default locale first (`SUPPORTED_LOCALES[0]`, the data's language); `readTexts` runs one `query.graph(…, { locale })` per locale for the batch's ids, selecting `categories.id`, `collection.id`, `tags.id`, `options.id` and `options.values.id` so the nested objects come back translated (ADR 0002, "Found on the way" 2); `toSearchText` joins every locale's title, description, category names, collection title, tags and option values, one line each, each line once.
- **Events.** The index lists `translation.created`, `translation.updated` and `translation.deleted`, and `product-collection.updated` and `.deleted`. `resolveTranslationProductIds` reads the event's translation rows (`withDeleted` for a deletion: the row is soft-deleted by then) and maps them by `reference`: `product` directly, `product_category`, `product_collection`, `product_option`, `product_option_value` and `product_tag` through `resolveProductIds`, which gained the collection case. A product is listed once however many of the event's rows touch it.
- **The middleware** (`src/api/store/search/locale.ts`, after `configureStoreSearch`): `chooseSearchLocale` keeps `req.locale` only if it is one of the store's `supported_locales` (compared without case; read once per request), else the default locale; `localizeSearchBody` removes whatever `search_options.locales` the caller sent and, for an index whose provider takes query-time locales (an allow-list, `meilisearch` for M6, so an unknown provider gets none and fails safe), writes `[locale]`. The store's locales come from the same `storeLocales` the transform uses. Every query of a multi-query body is handled by its own index.
- **The bulk rule.** Each translation row emits its own event, and each event re-reads its products in every locale, so a bulk change of translations (M4's sync, a CSV import) ends with `container.resolve(Modules.SEARCH).reindex({ index: "product" })`. From a shell, `medusa exec` a script that does that, or restart the server after `medusa db:migrate` when the schema changed.
- **An existing database.** The schema changed, so after pulling this: `pnpm --filter @shopblok/backend exec medusa db:migrate` ("Rebuilt following search indexes", 10 s), then start the backend, which seeds the new version and makes it live. A fresh database gets it from `pnpm bootstrap`.

### Measured

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Reindex of the demo catalog (8 products, four locales) at `medusa develop`'s start | `8 documents synced in 1s`, server up after 8 s |
| `search-locale.spec.ts` | 18 tests, about 17 to 21 s on its own (24 s in a full run); the slowest event path is under 0.7 s |
| `backend-integration` locally (both specs) | 22 tests, 40 s including the runner's two boots |
| Unit tests (`pnpm --filter @shopblok/backend test`) | 101 tests, 5 s |

### The suite and its mutations

The tests keep the ADR's numbers. **T1** (a reindex writes every store locale: each language finds the shirt by its own words, the sweater by none of them; translated category names are searchable; `search_text` is not on a hit, the English title, category, and the ids are), **T2** (accents, tonos and capitals), **T3** (informational: A′ leaks by design), **T4** (the events: a product title's and a category name's `translation.updated`, a tag's `translation.created`, a `translation.deleted`, each within 10 s over the in-memory bus), **T6** (hits translated and priced by one `/store/products?id[]=` call with the header), **the facets** (`category_ids` 1 + 1, `collection_ids` 2, four `option_value_ids` of 1, the category ids labelled in Greek by `/store/product-categories`, a facet id narrowing the hits), **T9 with T7** (`pt-BR` and `mn-MN` added to the store and translated, then found by `Camisa`, `linho`, `Маалинган`, `цамц`, `МААЛИНГАН`, with no restart), **T10** (the header alone; a caller's `locales` dropped, which Postgres would refuse; and, with the index reported as served by another provider and `query.search` spied, the locale sent, the fallback for `zz-ZZ`, `it-IT` and none, and the caller's `locales` overwritten).

Each mutation was applied, the spec run, and the change reverted (`git checkout`):

| Mutation | Failed |
|---|---|
| the three `translation.*` events left out of the index's list | the four T4 tests and T9 (10 s time-outs) |
| the text read selects `categories.name` without `categories.id` | T1's category names, T4's category name |
| the middleware lets the caller's `locales` win | T10 "overwrites the caller's locales" |
| the middleware keeps a caller's `locales` for Postgres | T10 "drops a caller's search_options.locales" (HTTP 400) |
| the middleware uses `req.locale` unchecked | T10 "falls back to the default locale" |
| the middleware not wired in `middlewares.ts` | T10's four middleware tests |
| `search_text` built from the default locale only | 12 tests: T1, T2, T3, T4, T6, T9, T10 |
| a deleted translation read without `withDeleted` | T4 `translation.deleted` |
| tag translations not mapped to products | T4 `translation.created` on a tag |
| no `option_value_ids` | the facets test |
| category names instead of ids in `category_ids` | T1's hit document, both facet tests |
| `search_text` retrievable | T1 "search_text is never returned" |
| one locale's texts per product (the last read wins) | 12 tests |

T2's folding is the provider's text-search configuration (`unaccent`, then English), which the assumptions spec's Greek test guards on Medusa's side; ADR 0002's mutation (`simple` without `unaccent`) is not repeated here.

### Where it differs from the plan

1. **The middleware does not write `locales` for Postgres.** D63 says it overwrites `search_options.locales` with `[locale]`; `search-postgres` refuses any query with `locales` ("does not support query-time locales", the assumptions spec's first test), so every search would be an HTTP 400. It removes the caller's `locales` for every index and writes `[locale]` only where the index's provider takes them, which is ADR 0002's decision 4 ("`locales: [locale]` for Meilisearch, nothing for A′"). The choice is per index, from `searchModule.getIndex(entity).provider` against an allow-list; M6 checks that its provider's registration id starts with `meilisearch`.
2. **Collections.** The plan names `product_collection` among the translated references but not among `search_text`'s texts; the collection title is in `search_text`, and `product-collection.updated` and `.deleted` are listed, so a renamed collection re-indexes its products.
3. **Coalescing.** The index's `consume` gets one event at a time (`graphConsume`), and `batchTranslationsWorkflow` emits one event per row (ADR 0002, "Found on the way" 3), so products are deduplicated within an event, not across a batch of events. The cross-event half needs a debounce outside the Search Module; the bulk rule above is what covers it.
4. **The assumptions spec** changed where T43 changed what it observed: the provider's refusal of `locales` is asked through `query.search` (the middleware now drops them before the route sees them); "`/store/search` ignores the request's locale, and the index holds the default language only" is gone, since this suite covers what replaced it; the event test listens with a subscriber of its own, since the index now subscribes to `translation.*` and `waitSubscribersExecution` returns the subscribers' results instead of the event body.
5. **The plan's "T2"** ("a translation update re-indexes") is in T4 here, under the ADR's numbering; T2 is the ADR's accents test.

### Smaller observations

- `query.search` and the Search Module resolved from the test container are the instances the route uses, so `jest.spyOn` on them sees what `/store/search` sends; that is how T10 checks the Meilisearch path on Postgres.
- The environment this ran in had no setup script (no preloaded images, no `/opt` sources, the docs domains blocked); the four images were pulled by hand and the Medusa facts were read from `node_modules/@medusajs/*/dist`.

### Review fixes (PR 71)

The review (`reviews/pr-71-code-review.md` in the project's files) found no blocker.

| Item | Fix |
|---|---|
| 1. Titles lost their ranking weight | `title` is searchable again with weight 3 (label A), beside `search_text` at 2 (B). A spec that a title match outranks a description that repeats the word did **not** tell the two apart: with and without the weight the shirt came first, so it is not in the suite. One reading: `ts_rank_cd` over the default-language title, which now sits in both fields, already favours it. Recorded, not settled. Also worth knowing for the instant search (T50 built it in M3, after this review): a query with `typo_tolerance: true` scores a hit `GREATEST(ts_rank_cd, word_similarity)`, and `word_similarity` is 1 for any text holding the exact word, so exact matches tie there whatever the weights |
| 2. Tags were a facet by value | `tag_ids` (from `tags.id`) is the facet, which the storefront labels in the visitor's locale; `labels` stays on hits. The tag test checks the facet, and a `toFacetIds` without tag ids fails it |
| 3. The provider check was a deny-list | an allow-list of providers that take `locales` (`meilisearch`); a mutation that adds `search-postgres` to it fails 16 of the 18 tests (every search is an HTTP 400) |
| 4. The middleware read the store's locales its own way, with a cache that never hit | it calls `storeLocales` from `search/helpers/translations.ts` (one read, trimmed, the default first); the `WeakMap` is gone |
| 5. `trimmed` copied three times | one, exported from `helpers/facets.ts` |
| 6. One store read per search | left: a 30 to 60 s module cache was to be weighed once the instant search existed. T50 built that search in M3 (the overlay asks `/next/search`, which is `cached()` a minute per market and query), so a repeated query no longer reaches this read; the cache stays a possible later task |
| 7. Sequential reads | the per-locale reads, the five reference lookups of a translation event, and the store's locales beside the pricing read all run side by side |

## Verification on the backend (T44)

Required e-mail verification (D64, SPEC §8.4) and the password reset e-mail, on the backend. The storefront's flow is T53's.

### How it works

- **`authVerificationsPerActor`** (`apps/backend/src/config/config.ts`): `customer: [{ entity_type: "email", auth_provider: "emailpass" }]`, always on, no env gate. An unverified customer's login answers `{ verification_required: true, verification, token }`, where the token has no actor.
- **The guard** (`apps/backend/src/api/store/customers/verified.ts`, wired on `POST /store/customers` in `middlewares.ts`): the account is created only for an auth identity whose e-mail has a verified `auth_verification`, and only under that e-mail: the route takes the customer's `email` from the body unchecked, so a verified login could otherwise create an account under someone else's address (PR 74's review, item 1). It reads the same rules from the config, so an identity from a provider no rule names (a social login later) is not held back. Refused: **403**, "Verify your e-mail address before creating your account." or "An account can only be created with the e-mail address you verified."
- **`auth.verification_requested`** (`src/subscribers/auth-verification-requested.ts`): for `entity_type: "email"` only, and only to an address the identity signs in with (Medusa does not check the request's `entity_id`, so any token could otherwise have the shop e-mail any address; review item 2), it sends `createNotifications({ to, channel: "email", template: "customer-verification", data: { url, code } })`. The local provider prints it in the backend's console (M3); Resend sends it from M6.
- **`auth.password_reset`** (`src/subscribers/auth-password-reset.ts`): for `actor_type: "customer"` only (an admin's reset has no storefront page), template `customer-password-reset`, `data: { url }`.
- Both send through `src/lib/storefront-mail.ts` (`sendStorefrontLink`), which takes the base from the config's `admin.storefrontUrl` (`STOREFRONT_URL`, mapped in `buildConfig`) and gives each e-mail an idempotency key (a hash of the code or the token), so a redelivered event sends nothing twice.
- **The links** (`src/lib/storefront-url.ts`): `{STOREFRONT_URL}{prefix}/verify?code=…` and `{STOREFRONT_URL}{prefix}/reset-password?token=…&email=…`. `prefix` is the request's `metadata.market`, **the market's public prefix** (`""`, `/us`, `/ch/fr`, what the storefront's `marketPrefix` gives), not its key: only the storefront has the market map. The prefix comes from the client, so only its shape is accepted (up to two lower-case segments of two or three letters); anything else gives the primary market's link, so a link cannot point at another host (`//evil.example.com` is refused). `STOREFRONT_URL` must be an http(s) URL; otherwise the subscriber logs an error and sends nothing.

### Measured (Medusa 2.21.2)

- **Medusa does not enforce by itself.** The restricted token from an unverified login, and the token `/register` gives, both created the customer through `POST /store/customers` (200) before the guard. SPEC §17.2's risk row now says so. The plan's fallback was the storefront's login action; the guard on the backend is stronger (it holds for any client), so T53's action does not need to enforce, only to handle the 403.
- **The verification event has a `code` and no separate token**, so the link is `/verify?code=…`, not the plan's `?token=…&code=…`. `POST /auth/verification/confirm` takes `{ code }` alone and allows an unauthenticated caller, which is what the `/verify` page needs.
- **A repeated `POST /auth/verification/request` keeps the first request's metadata** (a new code, the old `metadata.market`). The storefront's "send again" therefore links to the market of the first request: a shopper who first asked from `/us` and again from `/ch/fr` gets `/us/verify`. Accepted for M3; T53's `/verify` page can send the shopper on to their current market after confirming.
- **Accounts made before T44 must verify on their next login.** An emailpass identity without a verified `auth_verification` now gets `verification_required`, so `/store/customers/me` fails until it goes through `/verify`. Nothing is seeded with an account, so this only touches local databases with test accounts: recreate the account, or request a code (`POST /auth/verification/request` with the restricted token) and confirm it with the code from the backend's console.

### The suite and its mutations

`apps/backend/integration-tests/http/auth-verification.spec.ts` (5 tests; run with `pnpm --filter @shopblok/backend test:integration:http auth-verification.spec`): register, log in (`verification_required`), the restricted and the register tokens refused with 403, request with `metadata: { market: "/us" }`, the e-mail's link is `…/us/verify?code=…`, confirm with the code alone, log in again, `POST /store/customers` 200, `GET /store/customers/me` 200; a request without a market and one with `//evil.example.com` link to the primary market (a fresh identity each, because of the metadata note above); a verified login cannot create an account under another address (403); a request for an address the identity does not sign in with sends nothing; a customer's password reset with `metadata: { market: "/ch/fr" }` links to `…/ch/fr/reset-password?token=…&email=…`. Unit tests: `config.unit.spec.ts` (the setting's shape) and `storefront-url.unit.spec.ts` (prefixes, a base with a path, non-URL bases).

Each mutation fails the suite:

| Mutation | Fails |
|---|---|
| No guard on `POST /store/customers` | the account test |
| No `authVerificationsPerActor` | the account test |
| Verification sent on `channel: "feed"` | the account test |
| The market prefix left out of the link | the account and the reset tests |
| Any `/…` accepted as a prefix | the "not a prefix" test |
| The reset subscriber's actor check inverted | the reset test |
| The guard without the body's e-mail check | the account test |
| The verification subscriber without the own-address check | the "no e-mail for an address" test |

### For later

- **Rate limiting (M7, SPEC §6.2, §11.2):** `/auth/customer/emailpass/register`, `/auth/customer/emailpass` (login), `/auth/customer/emailpass/reset-password`, `/auth/verification/request` and `/auth/verification/confirm` are the routes to limit.
- **T53** passes `metadata: { market: marketPrefix(market) }` to `sdk.auth.verification.request` and to `sdk.auth.resetPassword`, reads `code` on `/verify` and `token` and `email` on `/reset-password`, and shows the notice when `POST /store/customers` answers 403.

## The data layer (T47)

**Result: the storefront has its data layer (D60): every read and write the pages of T48 to T53 need, as DTOs, the mappers to the registry's view models, the server actions behind one `action()` wrapper, `/next/visitor` and `/next/cart`, the island that fills the visitor store after hydration, and `/` redirecting to the market a visitor chose.** Against the dev stack, `curl` with a cart cookie shows `/next/visitor`'s count follow each add (0, 2, 3), `/next/cart` answers the cart with its options in Greek, both say `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, and `/` with `_shopblok_market=en-us` answers 307 to `/us`. The wiring page is unchanged. `pnpm build` passes with the stack and with no `.env`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Date | 2026-10-26 |
| Branch | `claude/project-thread-bbr2fk`, from `main` at `7e58444` (PR 71 merged) |
| New | `apps/storefront/src/lib/medusa/{cookies,cart,customer,orders,categories,collections,search,fulfillment,payment}.ts`, `src/lib/view-models/{common,product,cart,category,address,facets}.ts`, `src/lib/actions/{action,cart,cart-handlers,market,market-handlers}.ts`, `src/lib/{cookie-names,market-context,cart-view}.ts`, `src/lib/markets/suggest.ts`, `src/lib/visitor/{handlers,source,visitor-source}.ts(x)`, `src/app/next/{visitor,cart}/route.ts`, `src/test-support/{cookie-jar,medusa-wire}.ts`, and a test file beside each new module |
| Changed | `src/lib/cache.ts` (`CATALOG_LIFE`, `tagsFor`), `src/lib/medusa/products.ts` (`getProduct`, `listProductsByIds`, `listProductHandles`, `listOptionValueLabels`), `src/lib/visitor/store.ts` (`customer`, `suggestion`), `src/lib/markets/proxy-response.ts` and `src/proxy.ts` (the chosen market), `src/test-support/medusa-fetch.ts` (records the method and the body) |

### How it works

- **Cookies** (`lib/medusa/cookies.ts`, names in `lib/cookie-names.ts` so the proxy can read one without `server-only`): `_medusa_jwt` and `_medusa_cart_id` httpOnly, `lax`, 7 days; `_medusa_pending_customer` `strict`, 1 day; `_shopblok_market` `lax`, 1 year; all `secure` in production and `path: /`. `getAuthHeaders()` is `undefined` without a token (dtc-starter's `{}` was truthy, SPEC §8.2), so every customer read returns `null` without calling Medusa.
- **Catalog reads** are `cached()` with D58's `catalog` profile (`CATALOG_LIFE`: stale 5 min, revalidate 1 h, expire 30 days) and its tags: `getProduct(handle, { regionId, locale })` (tags `medusa:products` and `product:{handle}`), `listProductsByIds(ids, …)` (the search's hits, the cart's lines; the order asked for, unknown ids dropped), `listProductHandles(limit)` (handle order, for the PDP's `generateStaticParams`), `listCategories(locale)` (the tree from `parent_category_id`, by `rank`; tags `navigation` and `search` too), `listCollections(locale)`, `listOptionValueLabels(locale)` and `searchProducts(input)`. `cached()` gained `tagsFor(...args)`: tags worked out from the call's arguments, so a per-handle tag needs no wrapper per handle; they reach the one `"use cache"` function as arguments, as the fixed tags always did, so the key is unchanged in kind.
- **Search** (`lib/medusa/search.ts`): `searchBody(input)` is the plain body of `POST /store/search`: `q` when there is a query, the filters ANDed (`$and`), the values of one facet ORed (a list), one `option_value_ids` clause per option so colour and size AND, the price on `min_price_<currency>`, `on_sale_<currency>`, the sorts (`relevance`, `newest`, `price-asc`, `price-desc`, `title`; `newest` when there is no query), and the facets with `disjunctive_facets: true`. The locale goes in `x-medusa-locale` only; the body never carries `search_options.locales` (T43's middleware owns it). `toSearchResult` keeps the ids in order, the total, the page count, the counts and the price range. Checked on the stack: `$and` of a category and a price narrows to 4, `disjunctive_facets` still counts the other category.
- **Cart** (`lib/medusa/cart.ts`): `getCart(locale)` (`null` for no cookie, a 404 or a completed cart), `getOrCreateCart({ regionId, locale })` (creates with the region and the locale in the key's sales channel and sets the cookie; moves a cart of another region or locale instead of replacing it, D65), `addLine`, `updateLine` (0 removes), `removeLine`, `applyPromoCode`, `removePromoCode`, and for T52 `setEmail`, `setAddresses`, `setShippingMethod`, `initiatePayment` (the provider's own pending session, not `payment_sessions[0]`) and `completeCart` (clears the cookie on an order). Every write asks for `CART_FIELDS`, so its answer is the whole cart, and a write without a cart cookie fails before Medusa is called. `getCartItems()` reads only the lines' ids, variants and quantities, for the actions' checks.
- **Customer and orders** (`customer.ts`, `orders.ts`, for T53): `getCustomer`, the address writes, `login` (dtc-starter's `completeLogin`: `verification_required` sends the verification request with `metadata: { market: prefix }`, the market's public prefix as T44 expects; a token with no customer creates it from the pending cookie, treats T44's 403 as "not verified", logs in again and only then sets the JWT cookie, then moves the guest cart), `register`, `confirmVerification`, `requestPasswordReset`, `resetPassword`, `logout` (clears the JWT and the cart cookie), `listOrders(page)`, `getOrder(id)` (checks `customer_id` against the signed-in customer as well as Medusa's scoping) and the three transfer calls. `fulfillment.ts` and `payment.ts` list a cart's shipping options and a region's providers.
- **View models** (`lib/view-models/`): pure functions from DTOs to the registry's contracts, the market's URLs passed in (`Hrefs`): `toProductCard`, `toProductDetail`, `toCart`, `toCategories`, `toAddress`/`toAddressInput`, `toFacetGroups`. Money is upper-cased and never divided; a product with no price in the region has no card and no page; a product page keeps only the variants that name one value of each option; an option is a colour or a size when its title is one of the four catalogs' words for it (folded, so `ΧΡΩΜΑ` and `Größe` match), anything else draws as pills.
- **Actions** (`lib/actions/`): `action(schema, handler, { auth })` parses the input with zod (an object from a client call, or `(previousState, formData)` from a form), maps the issues to T34's kinds per field path (`required`, `pattern`, `invalid`), re-reads the customer from the JWT cookie for `auth: "customer"`, and answers `{ ok: true, data }` or `{ ok: false, errors, form?, message? }`: `ActionError`'s reason, `not-found`/`unauthorized` for Medusa's 404/401, `rejected` with Medusa's own words for another refusal, `unavailable` for an outage; anything else is thrown to the error boundary. The `"use server"` files (`cart.ts`, `market.ts`) export one async function per action; the bodies are in `*-handlers.ts`. `addToCart`, `updateCartLine`, `removeCartLine`, `applyPromo`, `removePromo` take `{ market, … }`, check the market against the map (`getMarketContext`), check that a line id is in the visitor's own cart before any write (SPEC §11.1), call `updateTag("cart")` and answer `{ count, cart }` (`addToCart` also `line`) as view models. `rememberMarket({ market })` keeps an open market's key in `_shopblok_market`.
- **Route handlers:** `GET /next/visitor?market=&path=` answers `{ cartCount, customer: { firstName } | null, suggestion }`, `GET /next/cart?market=` the `Cart` view model or `null` (404 for a market that is not open), both `private, no-store`, 503 when Medusa is down. The suggestion (`lib/markets/suggest.ts`): the `x-vercel-ip-country` country's market in the best `Accept-Language` match among its languages (else its default), on the same page (`path`, resolved to the path inside the market), `null` without the header, for a country the shop does not sell in or that has no region, for the visitor's own country, and whenever `_shopblok_market` exists.
- **The island:** `loadVisitor(market, path)` (`lib/visitor/source.ts`) asks `/next/visitor` once and calls `setVisitor`, keeping the consent the visitor gave on the page; a failed or malformed answer leaves the store "unknown", so the header keeps its placeholder. `VisitorSource` runs it in an effect; T48's layout draws it. `Visitor` has `customer` and `suggestion` beside `cartCount` and `consent`; `setVisitor` defaults both to `null`, so the DS fixtures and the tests that name only the first two did not change.
- **`proxy.ts`:** `/` itself, on a GET or HEAD, with `_shopblok_market` naming an open market other than the one `/` shows on that host, answers **307** to that market's root (the query kept), when that root is on the same host. A market on another host is not followed: each host has its own cookie, so two domain markets could each name the other and bounce forever (review item 1); there the suggestion banner offers it. Every other URL is served as before, whatever the cookie says.

### Where it differs from the plan

1. **`cached()` takes per-call tags** (`tagsFor`). SPEC §8.3 says "tags are fixed when `cached()` is called, so a tag per language needs one wrapper per language"; D58's `product:{handle}` would then need a wrapper per product. The tags are computed from the arguments before the `"use cache"` function and passed to it, as the fixed tags are. T56 corrects §8.3's sentence.
2. **The suggestion's shape.** D60 writes `suggestion: { market, href } | null`; MarketSuggestionBanner needs the country, the language, its tag and the currency (the registry's `MarketSuggestion`), so `/next/visitor` answers that contract with the market's key added. The island sends the page's public `path` so the link is the same page in the other market. The contract refuses a suggestion in the visitor's own country, so a visitor in Switzerland reading French on `/ch` gets no banner; the switcher covers that.
3. **A cart line's options come from its product.** The Store API's cart refuses nested variant fields (`*items.variant.options` answers the variant without them, checked with `curl`), and the line's `variant_title` is the default language's (`S / Black` in a Greek cart). So `/next/cart` and the actions read the lines' products with `listProductsByIds` in the market's region and locale (one cached read, the ids sorted) and take the options, the picture and the stock from there.
4. **Option value labels come from the products.** `/store/product-options` does not translate in 2.21.2 (`x-medusa-locale: el-GR` answered `Color`/`Black`, while the same values on `/store/products` are `Χρώμα`/`Μαύρο`), so `listOptionValueLabels(locale)` reads every product's options, 100 at a time, once per locale, cached with the catalog's life. A shop with thousands of products may want a cheaper source in T50 or M6.
5. **No tag facet group.** `tag_ids` is counted, but the Store API has no translated tag list to label it, so `toFacetGroups` draws categories, collections, each option (colours as swatches), the price and the sale toggle. T50 decides whether tags need a group.
6. **Images have a fixed size.** Medusa stores no width or height, and the contracts need both: every product picture is drawn as 1200 × 1600 (the fixtures' 3:4), and a product with none gets a grey 3:4 data-URI placeholder with an empty `alt`.
7. **"Low" is under 5.** D61 names "low" but no number; `LOW_STOCK_BELOW = 5` in `products.ts`, for tracked variants only (an untracked or backorder variant is never low or out).
8. **The curl check's add went through the Store API**, with the storefront's cookie set to that cart: no page imports the actions yet, so they are not in the build's server reference manifest and cannot be posted to. The action's own path (create, cookie, answer) is covered by the unit tests; T48's `shell.spec.ts` adds a line through the action's form.
9. **Customer, orders, fulfillment and payment are written, not exercised.** They type-check against the SDK and follow dtc-starter's flow with T44's facts (the prefix as `metadata.market`, the 403 until verified), but nothing calls them before T52 and T53, whose specs test them against the stack.
10. **`Address.city`** is optional since T45 (PR 72), so `toAddress` leaves it out for a saved address without one, as it does the other empty optional fields.

### Code review (PR 73)

The review (`reviews/pr-73-code-review.md` in the project's files, not in the repository) had ten items; all ten are fixed in this PR. Two were checked on the dev stack first, with a throw-away product and promotion that were deleted afterwards: Medusa adds a repeated variant to its line (an add of 2, then of 98, made one line of 100), and it compares promotion codes exactly (`t47probe` is "invalid" while `T47PROBE` exists and applies). A third was checked too: a product deleted after it was added keeps its line's `product_id`, `variant_id` and `product_handle`, so `toCartDto` keeps that line and it can be removed; only a line with no variant at all (a custom line, which this storefront never makes) is left out of the view.

| Item | Fix | Test (each fails with the fix undone) |
|---|---|---|
| 1. `/` could bounce between two domain markets | `chosenMarketRedirect` follows the cookie only to a root on the same host as the market `/` shows | proxy-response: example.com with `de-ch`, shop.ch with `el-cy` and `en-us` are not redirected; shop.ch with `fr-ch` still is |
| 2. A line the view leaves out could not be removed | `requireLine` checks `getCartItems()`, every line Medusa holds | cart-handlers: a line with no variant is removed |
| 3. A failed cart transfer failed the login after the JWT was set | `login` answers `signed-in`; a transfer Medusa refuses drops the guest cart's cookie, an outage keeps it for the next login | customer: a 400 from the transfer |
| 4. The 99 limit was the add's | `addToCart` refuses an add that takes the line past `MAX_LINE_QUANTITY` | cart-handlers: 2 + 98 is refused with no write, 2 + 97 passes |
| 5. The promotion check ignored case | exact comparison, as Medusa's | cart-handlers: `welcome10` against `WELCOME10` is rejected |
| 6. The badge could show an old count | `setCartCount` makes an unknown visitor known with its count; `loadVisitor` keeps a count set while its request was out | store: an add before the first answer; source: an add while the request is out |
| 7. The cart's stock came from a cached set of ids | `cartView` reads its products uncached (`readProductsByIds`): a cart is per visitor, and a revalidation by handle would not reach the cached set | none: the cache is Next's, which the unit tests stub |
| 8. A cookie for a closed market blocked the suggestion | the cookie counts only when it names an open market | handlers: `en-zz` in the cookie, the US suggested |
| 9. A selected value without a count dropped out of the sidebar | it stays in its group with 0 | view-models: a selected category and colour the search did not count |
| 10. A stepper click read the whole cart first | `requireLine` reads `getCartItems()` (`items.id,items.variant_id,items.quantity`), not `CART_FIELDS` | covered by item 2's test |

### Smaller observations

- The SDK writes a list as `id[0]=…&id[1]=…`; Medusa reads it as `id[]`.
- An unknown promotion code is Medusa's 400 (`The promotion code NOPE is invalid`), which `applyPromo` answers as `rejected` with that message; the action also refuses an answer with the code not applied.
- `prettier --check` with no `--config` reports every file: the config is `packages/config/prettier.config.mjs` (print width 100), which the editor integration finds and the bare CLI at the root does not.

## The shell (T48)

**Result: every market page now sits in the real shop around it (D66): the classic header with the navigation from Medusa's category tree, the search overlay, the account link, the market switcher and the cart's count, the multi-column footer, the suggestion banner and the cookie banner; the design system has a Templates group with `not-found` and `error`, and the market's 404 and error pages render them.** Against the stack, `shell.spec.ts` (7 tests) passes beside the other 93 browser tests, and every unit suite passes (storefront 93 files, ui 145, registry 13, fixtures 2, i18n 4).

### How it works

- **`site.ts`** is the shop's settings until M4's globals: the header (`classic`) and footer (`multi-column`) variant, the store's name, a sticky header, the announcement ("Free returns within 30 days", in the four languages) and the footer's columns (Shop: the top-level categories and "All products"; Help: account, cart, order lookup). `SHELL_PREFETCH` is `false` until the pages those links point to exist (a prefetch of a 404 is a console error on every page); the task that builds the last of them sets it to `null`.
- **`getShellData()`** (`components/shell/shell-data.ts`, React `cache`) reads the market, the market map, the category tree and the regions, all `cached()` entries, so the layout reads nothing per request. A Medusa error gives empty values (no navigation, no switcher) and the page is regenerated with them within the market map's 30 s life.
- **Navigation** (`lib/navigation.ts`): a top-level category with no children is a link; one with children is a mega menu whose columns are its leaf children in one column titled with it, then a column per child that has children (two levels; deeper ones are the category page's). Panels stay unmounted (D66). The seed's three flat categories are three links.
- **Search:** the header's new `search` slot takes `SearchOverlayIsland`, which waits 250 ms after the last key, aborts the question on its way, asks `/next/search?market&q` (T50's handler) and treats a 404, an answer that is not a result, or a refused request as "no results". The recent queries are `localStorage`'s (`recent-searches.ts`, eight at most, empty on the server). Enter still submits the overlay's GET form to `{m}/search`.
- **Switcher and banner:** `toMarketChoice` lists the open markets a country per row, each language a link to its market's home, leaving out a country Medusa has no region for (and the whole switcher when the current market's country has none). `MarketChoiceIsland` listens on the document for a plain click on a switcher link or the banner's "go", calls `rememberMarket` and then goes to the same page in that market (`samePageIn`: the path inside the market and the query, after the other market's home); "stay" records the current market. The banner is drawn by a server action (`renderSuggestionBanner`), called once the visitor store has a suggestion; the action works the suggestion out again from the request.
- **Templates:** `StatusPage` is what both share (the `<main id="main">`, a decorative icon, the one `<h1>`, a sentence, the ways on); `NotFoundTemplate` links home (primary) and to the search page; `ErrorTemplate` has a `retry` slot and links home. `as="div"` is for the design system, whose frame is the page's `<main>` already. The words are the catalogs' new `templates.notFound` and `templates.error`.
- **The 404 and error pages:** `not-found.tsx` renders the not-found template with the market's home and search links. `error.tsx` renders the error template with a "Try again" button that calls Next's `retry()`, the home link from `ShellLinksProvider` (the layout's; a client component reads no root param) and `unstable_rethrow` first. `SHELL_MESSAGES` is now the error template's four sentences (the wiring lines left it); the header's and the cookie banner's islands get their words as props.
- **Test hook:** `POST /next/e2e/cart?market=en-us&quantity=2` (404 unless `E2E_TEST_ROUTES=true`) puts that many of the catalog's first variant in the visitor's cart, so `shell.spec.ts` can check the header's count before any page can add to a cart.

### Where it differs from the plan

- **`/[market]` is not under 170 KB** (the plan's Verify). It was already 212 KB gzipped at T46 (the wiring page with the toast region and the cookie banner); the shell adds about 78 KB. Most of it is one shared chunk of Base UI (109 KB gzipped: the navigation menu, the dialogs of the mobile drawer and the search, the popover of the switcher). Removing the search island saved 0.6 KB only, so Turbopack's chunking, not one island, decides the number. `/[market]` is not budgeted; T49's product page is, and will meet this first (NEXT-SESSION.md, T49).
- **The cart drawer and the quick cart are T52's,** with the cart page: nothing can add to a cart before the product page, and T52 builds what opens them. The header's cart is the count's island.
- **The switcher's links are the markets' homes,** not the current path in each: the layout draws the switcher once for all the pages under it and knows no page's path. The island sends a click to the same page in the other market; without scripts the link goes to that market's home.
- **The banner is rendered by a server action,** so its copy and its markup stay on the server; the layout draws an empty banner so the action's answer can use the organism's client part (an action's answer can only use a client component the page's own server tree imports).
- **The count's test hook is a route under `/next/e2e`,** not a form posting to the add action: no page has an add-to-cart form before T49.
- **`SHELL_PREFETCH` is `false`** until the shell's links point to pages that exist.

### Smaller observations

- happy-dom follows a link while a click is still on its way to the document (`HTMLAnchorElement.dispatchEvent` navigates during the bubbling phase), where a browser waits for the end of the dispatch; `market-choice-island.test.tsx` routes anchors' `dispatchEvent` past it.
- Next 16.4's error boundary prop is `retry` (stable since 16.3); `reset` is still there for re-rendering without fetching.
- `pkill -f next-server` from a shell whose own command line holds the pattern kills that shell; stop the server by its PID (`ps -eo pid,cmd | awk '/[n]ext-server/{print $1}'`).

### CI fix (PR 75)

The first CI run's `design-system` job failed in `next build`: it builds with no `.env`, and the shell's category and region reads threw `EnvError` ("Medusa is not configured") while every market page was prerendered. Catching the error is not enough, because an error inside a `"use cache"` entry fails the prerender even when its caller catches it (reproduced in the VM with the `.env` moved away; the M0 wiring page never met it because it calls `connection()` first). `getShellData()` now asks `medusaEnv()` first and reads nothing from Medusa when it is not configured; the no-`.env` build with `DESIGN_SYSTEM_ENABLED=true` passes, and its design-system cells for the two templates pass except for the `en` pixel comparisons, which wait for the baselines.

### How it works

- **The page** exports `ensureStatic = "navigation"`. `generateStaticParams` goes through `prerender.ts`: with `MEDUSA_BACKEND_URL` set it asks for the first `STOREFRONT_PRERENDER_PRODUCTS` handles (500 by default) in handle order, and a Medusa that does not answer fails the build with a message naming it; without it (the design-system and `check` builds) it renders one placeholder, `__shopblok-stand-in__`, which the page answers with a 404 before it reads anything. A cap of 0 also renders the placeholder, because Cache Components refuse an empty list. The page reads the product (`getProduct`, tags `medusa:products` and `product:{handle}`), the related products (`searchProducts` on its first category, then `listProductsByIds`, the first eight but itself) and the messages, all `cached()`; `notFound()` comes first.
- **The template** (`ProductDetailTemplate`) is the page's `<main>`: breadcrumbs, then the gallery (11 parts) and the buy box (9 parts, sticky under the header) from `md`, then the information, the reviews (`#reviews`), the related carousel and the `recentlyViewed` slot. `slots.buyBox` and `slots.gallery` replace the two parts that follow the visitor; without them (the design system) it draws them from its values. `PRODUCT_DETAIL_IDS` names the form, the options, the button, the title and the reviews, so the sticky bar submits the buy box's form; the DS states pass their own ids.
- **The islands** (D61): each sits in a `Suspense` whose fallback is the server's buy box or gallery for the default choice, so the static HTML holds the default price, and reads `?variant=` with `useSearchParams()`. `BuyBoxIsland` writes a full choice into the URL with `history.replaceState` (no navigation; Next keeps `useSearchParams` in step), reads the URL again only when it names another variant than the one it wrote (a partial choice, which the URL cannot hold, is kept), adds through `addToCart` with `useActionState` (`adding` while it runs) and calls `setCartCount`, and draws the sticky bar for the current choice (`stickyFor`). `GalleryIsland` takes the choice the buy box publishes (`choice-store.ts`), so a colour alone already shows its pictures. `RecentlyViewed` remembers the page's card in `localStorage` per market (nine, newest first, links and pictures checked when read back) and draws the others.
- **The default choice** is the only variant for a one-variant product, nothing otherwise (add to cart waits for every option, SPEC §8.4).
- **Head:** the title is "{product} | Shopblok"; the description is the first 160 characters of Medusa's; canonical is the base PDP (`?variant=` is a choice, not a page); hreflang through `hreflangAlternates`; Open Graph with the first picture when it is a URL (not the placeholder). JSON-LD is a `@graph` of `Product` (one `Offer` per variant, availability from the stock) and `BreadcrumbList`, `<` escaped. `metadataBase` is `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`: a value that is not a URL throws, and a production build or server without one logs an error once and uses `http://localhost:8000` (CI builds with no `.env`, so it cannot fail there).
- **`/next/status`** is S4's variant C: a Store API read with the publishable key and a Payload `count`, 2 s each, side by side; 200 or 503, `no-store`, `{ status, checks: { medusa, payload } }`, the reason in the server log only.
- **`/api/revalidate`** takes `POST { tags, expire? }` with `Authorization: Bearer <REVALIDATE_SECRET>`, compares SHA-256 digests with `timingSafeEqual`, accepts only the catalog's tags (`medusa:{products,regions,categories,collections}`, `search`, `navigation`, `product|category|collection:{handle}`; never `global:markets` or the CMS's), and calls `revalidateTag(tag, { expire: 0 })` for `expire: 0`, `"max"` otherwise. 401 for a wrong or missing secret (and for every call while the secret is unset, with an error in the log), 400 for a body it does not know or one with no known tag. A tag it does not know beside known ones (a handle with a `.` or a non-ASCII letter, which Medusa allows) is skipped and named in the answer's `skipped`, which the backend logs; the rest are revalidated.
- **The subscriber** maps the event to tags (`RULES` in `lib/storefront-revalidate.ts`): a product's change refreshes `product:{handle}`, `medusa:products` and `search` with `"max"`; a variant's (the prices) refreshes the lists with `"max"` and its product's page with `expire: 0`, sent last; an inventory level's (the stock) only its products' pages with `expire: 0`, since a level changes on every order, or `medusa:products` with `"max"` when no product can be read; an option's, an option value's and a tag's the same as a product's for every product behind it, and a sales channel's deletion `medusa:products` and `search`; a category's and a collection's their handle, their list tag, `medusa:products` (the breadcrumbs carry their names), `search` (and `navigation` for a category); a translation's every text tag (its id names no product); a region's `medusa:regions`, `medusa:products` and `search` with `expire: 0`. The handles come from `query.graph` by id, deleted rows included; a deleted product or group uses its list tag. A failed read still sends the list tags; a failed POST is logged and never thrown (the event must not retry forever).
- **The job** `revalidate-catalog` POSTs `{ tags: ["medusa:products", "search"], expire: "max" }` every ten minutes (`*/10 * * * *`), for price lists, which emit no events.

### Where it differs from the plan

- **The PDP is 322.9 KB gzipped, not under 170.** The shell is 291.6 of it (T48's numbers); the page adds 31 KB (the gallery's and the carousel's embla, the buy box's radios and stepper, the zoom dialog). Steven raised the PDP's budget to 330 KB on 2026-10-26 (the `budgets` table in `scripts/first-load.ts`); the listing pages keep 170 KB.

## Listing pages and search (T50)

**Result: the shop has its listing pages and its search (D59, D63).** `{m}/store`, `{m}/categories/[...handle]` and `{m}/collections/[handle]` are in the static shell, paged by path (`/page/2`), each first page built for every category and collection; the filters and the sort are in the query and drawn by a listing island beside the server's results; without JavaScript the same forms land on `{m}/search`, which renders every filter and sort on the server; `/next/listing` and `/next/search` answer the island and the header's overlay. The listing pages are 318.6 KB gzipped, so their budget is 330 KB, like the PDP's (Steven's choice, 2026-10-26).

|---|---|
| Date | 2026-10-26 |
| Branch | `claude/project-thread-bbr2fk`, from `main` at `7192112` (PR 77 merged) |
| New (storefront) | `src/app/(storefront)/[market]/{store,store/page/[n],categories/[...handle],collections/[handle],collections/[handle]/page/[n],search}/page.tsx`, `src/app/next/{listing,search}/route.ts`, `src/components/listing/{listing-page,listing-island,robots-meta,remember-search}.tsx`, `src/lib/listing/{query,listing,handlers}.ts`, `src/lib/seo/listing.ts`, their tests |

### How it works

- **The routes** each export `ensureStatic = "navigation"` and render `ListingPage` (`components/listing/listing-page.tsx`) with their scope and the page from the path. The category route is a catch-all that reads a trailing `page/{n}` (`["apparel", "page", "2"]`); `store/page/[n]` and `collections/[handle]/page/[n]` are their own routes. `generateStaticParams` lists every category's path and every collection's handle (the first pages); the other pages render on their first request. `/page/1`, a page past the last, an unknown category or collection, the stand-in's placeholder and every listing in a build without Medusa answer 404, with `notFound()` before any `Suspense`. The paged routes list one placeholder (`/page/1`, a 404), because Cache Components refuse an empty list and `ensureStatic` wants every parameter.
- **The data** (`lib/listing/listing.ts`): `resolveScope` turns the scope into its title, trail and path in the market's language (a category through its path of handles in `listCategories`, with its descendants' ids as the search's filter), and `readListing` makes one `searchProducts` call (`cached()`, tags `search` and `medusa:products`), reads the hits through `listProductsByIds` and labels the facets' ids with `listCategories`, `listCollections` and `listOptionValueLabels`. The group the scope fixes (a category page's categories, a collection page's collections) is not offered. It builds the chips with their remove links, "Clear all" (which keeps the sort), the sort's options (relevance only with words), the forms' hidden fields and the empty states (no match with "Clear all", the search's "No results for …", an empty category with a link to the store). The page size is `STOREFRONT_LISTING_PAGE_SIZE` (24, 1 to 48).
- **The query** (`lib/listing/query.ts`, shared by the browser and the server): the forms' fields (`category`, `collection`, `opt_…` per option, `price.min`, `price.max`, `sale=1`), `sort`, `q`, `page` and `scope` (`category:apparel/tops`, `collection:summer-edit`, `store`). Ids, handles, pages and amounts that are not one are dropped. `filterParams` gives the filters and the sort in one sorted order, so equal choices give equal URLs.
- **The island** (`listing-island.tsx`) sits in its own `Suspense` with no fallback, before the server's results and never around them. It reads `useSearchParams()`; only when the query has a filter, a sort or a page does it ask `/next/listing?market&scope&page&…` and draw `ListingResults` in its root, which has `peer` and, once it has results, `data-active`, so the server's results (`peer-data-active:hidden`) are hidden by CSS. Once the query changes the results the server's are hidden at once: while the first answer loads the island says so, while a later one loads the last results stay, a 404 (no such page) is "no match" with a link back to the listing, and any other answer (503, no network) is "could not be loaded" with "Try again" (review item 1). Its pages' links keep the query (`?sort=…&page=2`). It catches a `submit` of any GET form whose action is the market's search page and whose hidden `scope` is its own (the sidebar, the drawer, the sort), drops the scope and the empty fields, and pushes the listing's URL (`history.pushState` on the same path, `router.push` from a `/page/n`): a new filter starts at page 1. It draws `<meta name="robots" content="noindex,follow">` with more than two facets (React hoists it into the head) and announces the count in a `role="status"` (4.1.3).
- **`{m}/search`** is dynamic: `searchParams` is read inside a `Suspense` whose fallback is the field and the heading, so the shell around it stays static. A `scope` from a listing's form keeps the search to that listing (and titles it with the listing's name); words title it "Results for “…”". It is `noindex, follow`, its metadata reads nothing from the URL, a page past the last shows the first, and it calls `rememberSearch` for the overlay's recent queries.
- **`/next/listing`** (`lib/listing/handlers.ts`): 400 for a scope that is none, 404 for a market, listing or page that is not there, 503 while Medusa is unreachable, else the `ListingResults` with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300` (the catalog's, not a visitor's).
- **`/next/search?market&q`**: the overlay's eight products, the matches' categories as links (most matches first, four) and suggestions from the matches' option values (three letters or more, not the query, four), `cached()` a minute per market and query (tags `search`, `medusa:products`).
- **Head and JSON-LD**: the title (", Page 2" after the first), a self canonical on every page by path (a filtered URL's canonical is its clean page), hreflang and Open Graph; JSON-LD is a `@graph` of `CollectionPage` with an `ItemList` (positions continue across pages) and a `BreadcrumbList`.

### Checks

### Code review (PR 78)

The review (`reviews/pr-78-code-review.md` in the project's files) had five must-fix items and one cleanup; all six are fixed, items 7 (a parent category whose handle is `page`) and 8 (the label reads after the search, not beside it) are skipped under the findings rule.

1. **A failed filtered load showed the unfiltered products.** The island now marks itself active whenever the query changes the results, so the server's grid is hidden from the first moment, and draws a loading line, "no match" with "Clear all filters" to the listing for a 404, or "The products could not be loaded" with "Try again" for anything else (new `templates.productListing.failed` in the four catalogs). Unit tests for the loading, 503, 404, bad body and network cases and the retry.
2. **A broken escape was a 500.** The second `decodeURIComponent` is gone (Next decodes params: `/us/products/demo%2Dheritage%2Dhoodie` is the hoodie), but Next itself answers a `URIError` in a dynamic route's params with a bare 500 before any page runs, the PDP's included (`/us/products/%ZZ` was a 500 too, with the PDP unchanged from `main`). The proxy now answers a path that does not decode with a plain 404, as `/next/missing-file` does; `proxy.test.ts` and `catalog.spec.ts` check it.
3. **`apparel%2Ftops` reached `apparel/tops`.** The routes build their scope with `categoryScope` and `collectionScope` (`lib/listing/query.ts`), which take only handles, so a segment holding a `/` is a 404; `parseScope` uses the same two.
4. **A filter without a chip left no way out.** The "no match" state always has "Clear all filters" (the listing with its sort only).
5. **`numberOfItems`** is the listing's total, which the positions run in.
6. **Cleanup:** one `categoryPaths` in `lib/medusa/categories.ts` (each node with its path) for the static params and the overlay's category links; `parseScopeKey` replaced by `parseScope`; `pathPage` uses `pageOf`.

The sort test also had a race of its own (it compared against a sorted copy of the prices read before the change landed), and the scripted filter test now waits for the island (drawn after hydration) before it ticks a box; each passed 6 runs in a row after.

## Home (T51)

**Result: each market's home is the shop's first page, built from Medusa's data in the static shell (D58), and the M0 wiring page is gone.** `{m}/` draws a hero (the shop's words from `site.ts` and a picture from `public/`, until M4's `hero` block), the top-level categories as tiles, the eight newest products as a carousel and a link to every product, with JSON-LD `Organization` and `WebSite` with a `SearchAction`. The wiring page's checks moved to the home: `<html lang>` and the switcher's current option, the carousel's prices in the market's currency and its titles in the market's language, and the `/next/markets` map.

| | |
|---|---|
| Date | 2026-10-26 |
| Branch | `claude/project-thread-bbr2fk`, from `main` at `6deced2` (PR 78 merged) |
| New (storefront) | `src/lib/view-models/home.ts`, `src/lib/seo/home.ts`, `public/home/hero.svg`, their tests |
| New (packages) | `packages/ui/src/templates/home.tsx` and its test, the `CategoryTile` and `HomePage` contracts, the `templates/home` entry (128 entries), `pageFixtures[locale].home`, the story |
| Changed | `src/app/(storefront)/[market]/page.tsx` and its test (replaced), `src/lib/site.ts` (`hero` per language, `HERO_IMAGE`), the four catalogs (`templates.home`; `wiring` removed), the fixtures' copy (`homePage`), `e2e/wiring.spec.ts` (rewritten), `e2e/markets.spec.ts`, the tests and comments that named `wiring` |

### How it works

- **The route** exports `ensureStatic = "navigation"`. Every read is a `cached()` entry: `listCategories` (tags `medusa:categories`, `navigation`, `search`), `searchProducts` (`search`, `medusa:products`) and `listProductsByIds` (`medusa:products`), so the build renders each market's home (`○ /el-cy`, `○ /en-us`, …) and the backend's revalidation reaches it. A market without a region, and every market in a build without `MEDUSA_BACKEND_URL` (the stand-in, D10), is a 404 with `notFound()` before anything renders, as the listings are.
- **The categories**: the first eight top-level categories in the navigation's order. A tile's picture is the newest product of the category or its children (one search, `pageSize: 1`), read through `listProductsByIds`; a product without a picture gives a tile without one (a muted frame, never the placeholder). The picture is decoration (`alt=""`): the tile is one link, named by the category.
- **The new arrivals**: `searchProducts` sorted `newest` (the index's `created_at`), eight, as ProductCards in the region's prices; "See all new arrivals" is `{m}/store` itself (its default order is the newest first, and `?sort=newest` would be a second URL the island fetches for). No category or no product leaves its section out, so an empty shop is the hero and the link to every product.
- **The hero** is `siteText(language).hero` (English for a language the shop has no text in) and `HERO_IMAGE`, an SVG under `public/home/` that next/image serves as it is. The section headings and links are the catalog's `templates.home` (the plan says `pages.home`; the templates' words are under `templates`, as the other pages' are).
- **Head**: the layout's default title (the store's name), the hero's line as the description, a self canonical, hreflang for every market's home, Open Graph `website`. JSON-LD is one `@graph`: the `Organization` (its `@id` the origin's, one for every market) and the market's `WebSite` with `inLanguage` and the `SearchAction` on `{m}/search?q={search_term_string}`.
- **The wiring page's facts**: market and language in `<html lang>` and the switcher's `aria-current` option, region and currency in the carousel's prices (all eight demo products, each against the seed's table), titles in the market's language, the map at `/next/markets`; the published-pages count goes to M4 (`countPublishedPages` stays in `lib/cms/site.ts`).
